17 Years Ago, Satoshi Nakamoto Opens His BitcoinTalk Account: What Happened Next

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On this day, 17 years ago, Satoshi Nakamoto opened an account on BitcoinTalk, the place that would become the home of early Bitcoin enthusiasts and then turn into a public forum for crypto in general, until social media platforms took over the internet.
  • The network itself was barely 1 year old, and its future raised more questions than answers.
  • Sources indicate that in 2010, the revolution began: 10,000 BTC was used to buy two pizzas, one of the first uses of the digital asset in exchange for a commodity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On this day, 17 years ago, Satoshi Nakamoto opened an account on BitcoinTalk, the place that would become the home of early Bitcoin enthusiasts and then turn into a public forum for crypto in general, until social media platforms took over the internet.

The network itself was barely 1 year old, and its future raised more questions than answers. Satoshi Nakamoto welcomed owners on the forum and invited any questions people had regarding the cryptocurrency.

Sources indicate that in 2010, the revolution began: 10,000 BTC was used to buy two pizzas, one of the first uses of the digital asset in exchange for a commodity. In May, Laszlo Hanyecz probably had the most expensive pizza dinner in history, considering how much BTC rallied after that. By December, Satoshi made their final BitcoinTalk post and announced their farewell.

According to recent reports, the 2011-2014 period turned out to be the foundation for the network as a whole. Bitcoin became an open-source project maintained by others. The first halving happened in November 2012 and reduced the block issuance from 50 to 25 BTC per block.

The first-ever exchange implosion, Mt.Gox in 2014, raised serious questions about the security and stability of centralized exchanges, an issue we haven't solved 17 years later.

2017-2021 were the years when the industry truly blossomed. We had our first bull run on Bitcoin, which pushed the price above expected levels, to almost $20,000 in December 2017, along with the first altcoin bull run and the birth of new technologies like smart contracts, NFTs and many more. The next cycle took Bitcoin to around $69,000 in November 2021.

Recent findings suggest that however, with the growth of the industry, multiple conflicts arose around safety, integrity and usage. The first country in the world to adopt Bitcoin was El Salvador, which implemented the digital currency as a true means of payment, in addition to accumulating it in its treasury.

2022 was the pivotal year, marked by the FTX and Terra crashes that changed how investors treat markets in general. FTX wasn't just an exchange: it was the backbone of the cryptocurrency market in those years. It aimed to rival Binance and become the bridge between institutional investors and crypto.

However, poor risk management, issues with fund allocation and many other factors caused an implosion that ended the bull run.

Recent findings suggest that in 2024, Wall Street arrived in crypto with ETFs, ETPs, perpetual futures and a regulatory framework. The digital assets industry became a part of a larger market. Whether that is good or bad is a question to consider, but one thing is clear: Bitcoin has come a very long way since 2010 and is evolving to this day.

In a recent development, the next step is the arrival of AI and rising cybersecurity risks, which go toe-to-toe with the quantum danger. How the first cryptocurrency handles them is a question that directly affects its future.

Inference now drives two-thirds of AI workloads, changing where chips get deployed

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (800 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that AI spending is shifting from giant training clusters toward smaller, promptly built sites, and modular data centers are becoming a natural home for inference workloads.
  • It has been revealed that inference-first chipmakers want to capture that shift.
  • “We’re at a point where about two-thirds of the workloads being run through these AI infrastructures are inference versus one-third is training.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 13:28 EST / NOVEMBER 21 2026.

It has been revealed that AI spending is shifting from giant training clusters toward smaller, promptly built sites, and modular data centers are becoming a natural home for inference workloads. Power, cooling and memory supply now shape where tokens get generated as much as raw chip performance does.

It has been revealed that inference-first chipmakers want to capture that shift. Positron AI Inc., which raised $875 million at a $5 billion valuation in September, builds inference appliances around commodity memory instead of scarce high-bandwidth memory. Inference has overtaken training as the force behind infrastructure buying decisions, according to Cameron McCaskill (pictured), head of sales and business development at Positron.

“We’re at a point where about two-thirds of the workloads being run through these AI infrastructures are inference versus one-third is training. And back in 2023, it was like 85% training, 15% inference,” McCaskill said. “So now you can see why inference is driving the economic decisions of how they’re going to build out their infrastructure.”.

McCaskill spoke with theCUBE Research’s Rebecca Knight and John Furrier at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed inference overtaking training, Positron’s commodity-memory chip design and why low-power modular data centers suit inference. (* Disclosure below.).

Positron’s first-generation Atlas server ran on a programmable chip, and the organization plans to tape out its own silicon early next year for its Titan server. Oracle Corp. is bringing about 340 Atlas servers live in its cloud this quarter, McCaskill noted. A neocloud provider has also signed on for Atlas and committed to Titan. Positron’s central design choice was skipping high-bandwidth memory.

“Everyone else pretty much in the industry is using what’s called HBM or high bandwidth memory. It’s very limited in supply, very expensive,” McCaskill said. “We went with commodity memory.”.

Recent findings suggest that that choice also keeps power low enough for air-cooled rooms. A single Positron server draws about 4,500 watts, and a full rack of Titan servers fits within 40 kilowatts, McCaskill explained. That footprint suits sites where operators can find a few megawatts of cheap power without heavy regulatory hurdles. For inference providers monetizing fresh capacity, deployment speed is a significant part of the appeal, according to McCaskill.

Recent findings suggest that “One of the groups of companies that we’re seeing a rise in right now and coming to us for product is these modular data centers, where they have a half megawatt or, 1 megawatt or 2.5 megawatt modular data center, and those can be deployed very promptly,” McCaskill noted. “And the goal of a lot of these inference players is I want to get from land and power to monetizable tokens within 90 to 120 days. And those modular data centers, coupled with our technology, can be a great solution.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • To leave, participants must voluntarily withdraw, be medically withdrawn by a DS (directing staff) due to injury or be dismissed for refusing a direct order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jumping out of a helicopter into water below, rappelling down a 22-story building, enduring chemical warfare gas exposure — if you’ve never seen Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test, these are just a few of the tasks that must be completed.

Sources indicate that it’s a reality TV show in which celebrities do physical challenges from the actual Special Forces selection process playbook. It’s like a competition show, but there are no eliminations, and no one gets voted off.

To leave, participants must voluntarily withdraw, be medically withdrawn by a DS (directing staff) due to injury or be dismissed for refusing a direct order. During the final test, the DS ejects those who fail the interrogation or selection test.

Season 5 is set in the Malaysian jungle. It features Candace Cameron Bure, Brandi Glanville, Oliver Hudson, Ruby Rose, George Santos, Bre Tiesi, Matt Barnes, and Mauricio and Alexia Umansky, among others.

At the time that this article was published, Alexia was still in the competition. Mauricio voluntarily withdrew after a rib injury sustained during a hand-to-hand fighting challenge with former NBA player Matt Barnes. Mauricio remarked the injury took two or three months to heal.

The following challenge involved gas, and Mauricio didn’t think his ribs could take it. He said he feared having a bad lung injury in the Malaysian jungle. Alexia agreed with the decision, saying the gas was the “most painful thing” she’d ever experienced in her life.

Inman spoke to Mauricio and Alexia midway through the season about the experience, the latest industry news and what’s next for The Agency.

What follows is the conversation, edited for length and clarity.

According to recent reports, I think for me, 100 percent, the heat. I think I anticipated intense heat and intense humidity, but you don’t know what it’s like until you really feel it … It was so unbearably hot, and in our barracks that we slept in, there was no windows, and when you were inside, you actually couldn’t tell like what was even happening out there. But it was almost like … “Good, let me be locked in this metal box because the outside is crazy.”.

It has been revealed that mauricio: I think for me, it was just the intensity of what a jungle really is. The first day we got there … when we were all showering and waiting to shower, there was a scorpion crawling on my leg, about to go in my boot, which I felt it and took it off just in the nick of time. Because if it went in my boot, it would have stung me, no question, right?

According to recent reports, alexia: It’s so hard to choose because literally every single thing was hard. Part of me wanted to say the car rides leading up to each challenge, because we didn’t know what was coming, and it was always so intense in the car. My heart would start pounding … the bottom line is the hardest part is just making sure that your mindset is correct [in] doing all these things and waking up each day and moving forward because that’s really what gets going is just moving forward and choosing to keep on going.

Mauricio: Yeah, I think Alexia nailed it. I mean, for me, it was really all about the little victories. The only way to survive is by looking at small victories, small steps … we used to say just make it to the next meal, just make it to the next day, just make it to tonight.

For me, the hardest part was leaving, was having to voluntarily withdraw. I did not want to have a medical withdrawal, so I didn’t want to go see the doctor and have them withdraw me.

Mauricio: Not one thing for me. What about you, Alexia?

It has been revealed that alexia: No. There’s nothing about this that’s easy.

It has been revealed that alexia: We loved everybody so much. I mean, we still talk all the time, and we still love each other so much. The words of affirmation we all told each other to this day are so special … But I think my first answer would have to be Candace [Cameron] Bure … she’s so strong, and we got looped together for a bunch of things because of our height similarities.

Mauricio: Well, I have to say that the person who surprised me the most was Alexia … the strength of her mind, her strength and what she did was extraordinary.

Alexia: Oh my god, yeah. Are you kidding me? All the time.

Alexia: Definitely thought it was pretty cool. It was an honor to be punched in the chest by DJ Tanner … I actually appreciated very much that she didn’t hold back because I just felt like I was treated like an equal, an individual.

Alexia: I’ve never punched anyone or anything … the second she threw the first punch, I knew she was so much stronger than me. But my goal was to just not fall down. I really didn’t want to fall down, so I was just trying to stay up the entire time. It felt like a fight went on for so long.

Pete Dadds / FOX. ©2026 FOX Media LLC.as.

Alexia: I had zero plans on talking about that while we were there. Before we go into the course, they make you talk to some psychologists … they do ask you before the show, “What’s the worst thing that you’ve ever been through?”.

And I remember thinking, like, “Are we gonna go there? … That would be so inappropriate. Everything’s in my power, and I’m not gonna go there” … Once I was finally in there, I understood why they asked … you’re stripped down to the very core of you, and you’re tired, and you’re pushing yourself, and you’re emotional, you’re exhausted … And Bre Tiesi, she got emotional, and [she mentioned to me] ”I haven’t cried in years. I hate crying.”.

It was really about discovering and repurposing the strength that I always felt that I had, but there was a time that I had felt that I had lost that.

And each night, as I was going to sleep, I just remember thinking to myself, “This is so rewarding, and this is so empowering, and this is so incredible for someone that has gone through what I have” … some people [feel like they] get their voice back. I always felt like I had my voice, but I feel like I got to discover a strength I always knew I had that someone had pushed me to question, and feeling that was just incredibly healing.

Alexia: No, not my parents. I had told two of my sisters before, and then, obviously, I told my dad on the course, and then, before the show aired, I ended up calling my mom and [sister] Portia to tell them because I obviously did not want that to be the first time they read it. And even though I spoke about it on the course, I’m still very, very afraid to tell them afterward, too.

Mauricio: It was extremely difficult … I was just proud of Alexia every single day, every single moment … hearing that story was just another revelation of her conquering and finally talking about something that I wish she never held back … I just wanted to reach out and just hug her. But by the same token, I also wanted to give her space and let her be her in that moment that she was sharing with everybody. So there was like a lot of stuff going through my mind.

There was anger toward this kid that did this … But [watching her let go of it] was beautiful to watch … from my perspective, it was like, “Do I reach over and become a dad and just give her a significant hug, or do I let her go through this moment, psychologically speaking, of letting it all come out?”.

And I was just proud of her all the way around.

In hindsight, I love that she was able to share that, get it off her chest with us, with everybody, with the world. I think it’s super powerful.

Sources indicate that pete Dadds / FOX. ©2026 FOX Media LLC.as.

Yes, I live by a lot of different small philosophies. Certainty versus doubt. Momentum is the cure of all fears. All of these are the different things where you just have to move forward, right? In order to accomplish something, you kind of just have to move forward, right? … the moment that I went from being an agent to opening up a brokerage, you jump off the cliff; you hope the parachute catches.

Industry observers note that to today … here we are in a really difficult real estate market. I mean, it is not fun out there right now whatsoever. Yet [The Agency is] still growing. We’re still putting money out there. We’re still doing things right. So yeah, to me that’s just a philosophy that I always live by.

It has been revealed that mauricio: I don’t know. We’ll just keep going. I really like that show Traitors. I would love to be on that show. That could be a fun one for me, so I’m putting that out into the universe.

Industry observers note that alexia: My dream would be to do a reality TV show with my family … We did Buying Beverly Hills, and we’ve done Real Housewives for like [16] years now. But we’ve never done something all of us together, just us, and I think that’ll be really cool.

It has been revealed that mauricio: I’m going to leave that one on the table. If anything, it’s for 2030. There’s still plenty of time to do that and make that decision. But I love LA, and I think I can help LA a lot. I think we live in an amazing city, and if the moment comes, and I’m set up in the right position in the business and I feel like I can actually win, I might do it. But I wouldn’t do it if I didn’t feel like I could actually win.

Recent findings suggest that mauricio: It’s an absolute mess, what’s going on in our in our in our industry right now, particularly with the listings. My take is, it’s quite simple. I think that there’s a lot of change that’s happening. I believe that it’s somewhere in the middle. Like I do everything.

I believe sellers should have choice, but I believe that we should be sharing those private listings amongst everybody — every agent, every brokerage firm, not just keeping it for themselves. I feel like there’s a lot happening right now in the industry where everybody’s really looking out for themselves: the MLSs, NAR, Compass.

According to recent reports, actually, Compass, I think, wants to collaborate, wants to share, but they’re in a massive, big fight. But in the meantime, this Clear Cooperation Policy is what is allowing them to keep all the listings to themselves and not share them … The PLS is exactly what that was, and I still think that if Clear Cooperation Policy didn’t pass, it would have been an amazing business to have right now.

Industry observers note that mauricio: We are really positioned as the premier luxury brokerage firm outside of Compass right now. They’ve got Sotheby’s, they’ve got Christie’s, they’ve got all of those different brands, and we’re the only independent luxury brokerage firm out there right now.

So I’m excited to be in that position. Competitors make you better every single day … I’m excited in terms of where we sit, where we stand in a very difficult time; I’m not excited about the market. We really need to do some things to improve it. We’ve had three years of very, very difficult conditions, and it’s going to be very difficult for people to survive. And those that do survive will come out better.

I think we’re in a good position to survive, but we’ve got our work cut out for us over the next year, year and a half. But we’ll continue to grow. We’ll continue to expand, and I’m excited to just be a part of this industry. But man, it’s hard out there right now.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul Signs New Private Listings Bill

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (663 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • New York has signed a new private listings bill, which means that properties will be required to be visible to the public as they hit the market unless the seller signs an informed opt-out consent.
  • Kathy Hochul signed the Fair and Transparent Real Estate Listing Act.
  • This follows a quick path through the state's Legislature, which approved the act in a noncontroversial vote in June.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New York has signed a new private listings bill, which means that properties will be required to be visible to the public as they hit the market unless the seller signs an informed opt-out consent.

Late last week, Gov. Kathy Hochul signed the Fair and Transparent Real Estate Listing Act. The language of the bill requires that real estate listings be marketed in "at least one other publication, platform or website that does not require payment" or for the consumer to work with the brokerage for access.

This follows a quick path through the state's Legislature, which approved the act in a noncontroversial vote in June. The New York State Association of Realtors® strongly supports the bill.

This becomes the latest crackdown on private listings, where a real estate agent markets a property to a limited list of buyers before making it public.

It has been revealed that fair housing advocates say private listings raise discrimination concerns. One study from Bright MLS found private listings take longer to sell and don't guarantee more money.

The listing must be accessible to the general public, "without limitation to a particular brokerage, franchise or select group of licenses." Also, there can't be restrictions on some or all of the details in the listing, according to the language of the bill.

The bill doesn't require a seller or lister to hold open houses or public showings if it violates any state or federal laws related to health and safety. And sellers can opt out, by signing a form that explicitly warns them that the listing will have limited visibility and possible impact on the price they get.

Upcoming York can punish violators with a fine of up to $5,000 and suspension or revocation of  their real estate license.

Earlier this year, the state saw its inventory of homes for sale fall to a 30-year low.

Washington and Connecticut have passed similar laws this year. Each has generally similar language in their bills, which also allow for opt-outs. A study from Zillow found the sales price of private listings was 1.3% less than comparable sales on the multiple listing service, costing the seller an average of $4,230 per sale. (Realtor.com® recently struck an agreement with Zillow to show preview listings from brokers who participate in Zillow’s preview program, in an effort to boost market transparency.).

Sources indicate that compass Inc., the real estate brokerage giant which has defended its use of private listings, said its recently unveiled See It First listings strategy complies with the law. It launched that program in September, which gives early access to homes that will soon be listed on the public market. Users don't need to work with a Compass agent to use it.

"New York’s new law preserves homeowners’ right to choose how they market their homes, including the ability to use a See It First strategy to test pricing and gauge demand," a Compass spokesperson remarked. "See It First early access homes comply with the new law and continue to give sellers flexibility in how and when they bring their homes to market.".

Sources indicate that new York has long struggled with housing affordability. The Realtor.com State-by-State Housing Report Card gave the Empire State an F, the lowest rating possible. Hochul has emphasized affordability concerns and made a deregulation push to make home construction easier.

“My administration is focused on making Upcoming York more affordable and liveable for every New Yorker regardless of age or income, and housing is central to that goal,” Hochul stated last week.

Tristan Navera is a senior reporter on housing policy, covering trends and solutions in the housing market from Washington, DC. He was previously a senior reporter at Bloomberg Law, and before that covered real estate for the Washington Business Journal. Earlier in his career, he spent a decade reporting on business and real estate in Dayton and Columbus, OH. A Cincinnati native, he holds a journalism degree from Ohio University.

Breaking: We keep coaching real estate agents to be salespeople. That was never the job

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (959 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, OPINION: Lance Pendleton argues that real estate agents are consultants, not salespeople.
  • Sources indicate that I was the national head of agent development at Compass, and I’ve been in front of more than 30,000 agents since.
  • According to recent reports, you didn’t fail the program.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, OPINION: Lance Pendleton argues that real estate agents are consultants, not salespeople. Learn what to ask before you pay for a coaching program.

Sources indicate that I was the national head of agent development at Compass, and I’ve been in front of more than 30,000 agents since. I’ve also sold the thing I’m about to take apart, so keep that in mind while you read.

According to recent reports, you didn’t fail the program. The program failed you. How come?

The reason is simpler than anybody wants it to be. Nearly every coaching program in this business teaches professional sales skills to people who are not in sales. We’re consultants, advocates, advisors and educators.

Nobody has ever talked a family into a house they didn’t want to live in. What we do is help people through the largest and most emotional decision of their lives with the least amount of damage. We read a room. We tell someone the truth about their kitchen, and we hold a deal together at 9 p.m. on a Sunday when the buyer’s father has opinions.

That is not selling. We’re consultants, advocates, advisors and educators. If you can fog a mirror, you can get a license. Very few people can do those four things well, and I’ve yet to see a program that teaches them as a skill set.

This isn’t the coach’s fault. Coaches were trained the same way the rest of us were. Build the database. Reach as many people as you possibly can. Add value, and then add more of it tomorrow.

It has been revealed that there’s a word buried in there that I think is the dumbest one in our industry, and I say that with love. Value.

Industry observers note that we all have the same value. Every one of us can pull a comp, open a door, write an offer and get to a closing table. What almost none of us have is a point of differentiation, the thing that tells a consumer specifically what you do for them and why it ought to be you. You can follow “add value” for a decade and stay interchangeable with the other four agents the seller interviewed.

There’s a second reason the homework never gets done: Agents live in two periods of time: now and not now.

According to recent reports, now is the pipe that burst three hours before a closing. Now is the appraisal, the inspection, the client calling at 10:30 p.m. about something that could have been a text. Now is loud, it’s permanent, and it pays this month. Not now is quiet and pays in three years, if at all.

The trouble is that everything producing long-term income security in this business sits in the not-now column. The National Association of Realtors’ 2026 member profile puts median gross income at $88,500 for agents with 16 years or more in the industry, and $8,000 for agents with two years or less.

The veterans report a median 49 percent of their business from repeat clients and another 32 percent from referrals. For the newest agents, both of those medians are zero.

Somebody will say that’s just arithmetic, that you need a past client before you can have a repeat one. That’s the point. The whole gap is 15 years of relationships, and not one hour of that work feels urgent on a Tuesday. This is a patient business being coached like an impatient one.

We do something else I think is worse. We coach in a permanent state of enthusiasm. Everything is fabulous; every market is an opportunity; you’re crushing it; this is your year. I call that toxic positivity, and it does real damage. You sit in a hard month with two deals coming apart, you hear all of it, and you quietly conclude the problem must be you.

What would help is unglamorous. This job burns through five things: prioritization, organization, time management, impulse control and emotional regulation. By Thursday of an ordinary week, most good agents are running low on at least two.

In a recent development, there’s nothing wrong with any of those people. Real support builds bumpers around those five, the same reason a bowling lane for kids has them. You don’t make the gutter disappear by concentrating harder.

That work means dealing with people as they are, for who they are. Not more, more, more. Not the next great thing. One thing, chosen for that person, small enough to start on a Thursday when everything else has gone sideways.

Sources indicate that we haven’t served this business well on that, and I include myself. I’ve sold the four-week cycle. It’s a comfortable thing to sell, because Week 1 always works.

It has been revealed that if you’re picking a program this fall, ask what gets cut. Anybody can hand you 15 things. The one worth paying is the person who tells you which one matters and which 14 you can skip.

We’re not in sales. We never were. Until the coaching in this business is built for that job, we’ll keep running very good people through programs that leave them feeling like the problem.

It has been revealed that you aren’t the problem. This is still the best time there’s ever been to be a great agent. We just have to stop training you for somebody else’s job.

The views and opinions expressed here are those of the contributor and separate from the Inman newsroom.

Recent findings suggest that lance Pendleton is the founder of Reframe Lab, a coaching and consulting practice for real estate agents, and the former national head of agent development at Compass in Connecticut. Get connected on Instagram.

Major crypto exchange Coinbase shared the options-implied seven-day ratios for major cryptocurrencies, highlighting that options traders might be preparing for an unusually large price move for XRP.

In an X post, Coinbase Markets shared the outcome of dividing the options-implied 7-day move by the median 7-day move for XRP, Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana.

Options-implied 7d move, divided by each asset's own median 7d move: $XRP 1.94× $BTC 1.69× $ETH 1.56× $SOL 1.46× $XRP is priced furthest above its own history, $SOL the least. Which one is asking for more than its own history delivered? https://t.co/WgWbqjcgwI.

This suggests how much movement options markets are pricing in relative to each asset's own historical behavior. However, it does not compare their expected dollar or percentage moves directly.

In a recent development, according to the figures shared by Coinbase, XRP's options-implied seven-day move stands at 1.94 times its own historical median seven-day move. Bitcoin follows at 1.69 times, while Ethereum records 1.56 times and Solana comes in at 1.46 times.

XRP, therefore has the highest relative reading among the four assets, suggesting options traders are pricing in a more pronounced move than the token has typically delivered over a comparable period.

Sources indicate that at the time of writing, XRP was down 1.93% in the last 24 hours to $0.98 amid the continued profit-taking in the market. XRP briefly reached $1 on November 18, 2026, but fell afterwards as traders took profits. XRP is down 21.57% so far in November, but its history claims more than its current price action does.

Industry observers note that XRP’s average November gain is skewed upward by massive outlier rallies—specifically +550% in 2013 and +282% in 2024. Its median November return is about -10%, meaning it has closed lower in most cycles in history. XRP dropped roughly 23.42% in November 2019 and lost 12.18% in November 2025 (opening at around $2.51 and closing at around $2.20).

A weak November doesn’t always mean a weak December: for instance, after falling 9.1% in November 2015, XRP jumped 46.8% in December 2015.

In the near term, XRP’s price recovery will target $1 before moving to the $1.24–$1.26 range. Alternatively, if the price falls further, it is likely to find support at $0.89.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:48 EST / NOVEMBER 21 2026.

Sources indicate that A sovereign AI factory is only as valuable as the companies that can actually get onto it. Across Europe, publicly funded AI factories are racing to give startups and small manufacturers supercomputer-class GPUs without pushing them into lock-in or loose data handling.

In Stuttgart, the HammerHAI AI factory is taking shape around a system from Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. using Nvidia Corp. Grace Blackwell chips. The center’s pitch leans as much on people as on processors, according to Bastian Koller (pictured), managing director of the High-Performance Computing Center Stuttgart.

“It’s very vital to bring them there because everybody’s talking about AI, but we focus especially on SMEs and startups,” Koller said. “So some startups know what they want, some startups want to try and they need help and support.”.

Koller spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Amit Eyal Govrin at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how HammerHAI avoids lock-in, its pragmatic approach to sovereignty and a concierge model that pairs each customer with a consistent contact. (* Disclosure below.).

In a recent development, industrial consumers no longer want shell programming; they expect the look and feel of a hyperscaler, which raises fresh demands on security and access. The center has already worked with customers on existing systems while it waits on the newly introduced hardware, and several have produced success stories. Rather than holding onto them, it designs its services so workloads can leave, according to Koller.

Recent findings suggest that “The idea is to evolve the system and the services in a way that they can simply move from us to a hyperscaler or from hyperscaler back,” Koller said. “Because what we are doing is, we give them a boost, we push them forward.”.

That pragmatism extends to sovereignty itself. The Stuttgart center runs an ISO-certified environment with TISAX Level 3 certification for automotive work. Full independence, down to European chips, is not realistic in the near term, Koller explained.

Industry observers note that “We cannot now say, okay, come back in 10 years when we have a sovereign processor or a sovereign GPU or something like this,” Koller said. “We have to look for the data.”.

Efficiency is part of the equation, too. The newly introduced system doubles the performance of its 3.2-megawatt predecessor at about 700 kilowatts, and the center reuses its waste heat. The bigger lesson is human: A concierge model pairs each customer with a consistent contact, according to Koller.

Recent findings suggest that “We learn more how the people are working and thinking, to be honest,” Koller noted. “… We can build up a system which is highly fancy, whatever there, nobody will use it because we never thought about what the user needs.”.

Industry observers note that on Nov. 18, Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid to its list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms. The listing covers the web interface of the Hyperliquid trading terminal at app.hyperliquid.xyz/trade. The HYPE token dropped to around $65.50 on the evening of Nov. 18, and it recovered to $68.79 by midday Nov. 19, according to TradingView data.

According to the entry, the tech giant claims to provide digital asset trading services on the website, and it has no address on record. Hyperliquid is not licensed by the SFC, and it is suspected of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong or actively promoting its services to the public, the regulator remarked.

In an accompanying warning, the SFC reminded investors that such platforms often lure people with "incredible investment opportunities." The SFC also reminded investors that clients of unlicensed platforms have no legal protection if a platform is hacked or misappropriates their assets.

On the same day, the Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the U.K. Financial Conduct Authority with seven recommendations on the country's new crypto rules. "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity," the group wrote.

On Nov. 16, two days before the SFC added Hyperliquid to the list, Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan spoke at the Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum. "Before the end of this year, we will introduce a bill to complete the regulatory perimeter," Chan said.

According to Chan, the bill will cover crypto dealers, custodians, advisers and asset managers. "Decentralisation does not mean less accountability," he noted.

In April, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority licensed HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial as the first stablecoin issuers in the city, out of 36 applicants in the first round.

Latest Update: Tech Roundup: Zillow Preview listings go live in RealScout

💡 Key Takeaways

  • This week’s Inman Tech Roundup covers Lofty’s newly introduced monthly index, which tallies how much time its AI saves agents, a $1.65 billion October for proptech funding, Airbnb’s early-2027 launch window for its AI travel agent and Zillow Preview’s new home inside RealScout.
  • Recent findings suggest that lofty is launching the Lofty AI Index for Real Estate, a monthly report tracking how much time its AI tools save real estate agents.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Can AI time savings be measured? Lofty is trying. Plus: $1.65 billion in October proptech funding, Airbnb’s AI travel agent and Zillow Preview in RealScout.

This week’s Inman Tech Roundup covers Lofty’s newly introduced monthly index, which tallies how much time its AI saves agents, a $1.65 billion October for proptech funding, Airbnb’s early-2027 launch window for its AI travel agent and Zillow Preview’s new home inside RealScout.

Recent findings suggest that lofty is launching the Lofty AI Index for Real Estate, a monthly report tracking how much time its AI tools save real estate agents. The inaugural edition found Lofty AI products, including Lofty Cowork, completed 1.13 million tasks in October, saving real estate agents 131,248 hours.

The index counts tasks Lofty’s AI completed, such as follow-ups, social media posts, homeowner check-ins and CRM updates, then estimates how long each would take an agent to do manually.

Among the findings: 387,824 leads got an AI follow-up text or email; solo agents saved 30 percent of their hours on daily planning; and agents in Michigan saved more time than any other region.

“Every AI vendor touts the time-saving nature of their AI product, but almost none of them show the data to confirm that what they say is true. We decided to cut through the smoke and mirrors around AI results and create measurable clarity with the Lofty AI Index. Each month we’ll put a number to the AI impact, show the calculations and stand behind it,” mentioned Joe Chen, CEO of Lofty.

It has been revealed that the time-saved figures rest on the company’s own estimates of manual task times, and the release doesn’t say how many agents are behind the totals, which makes per-agent impact hard to gauge. Since this is the first edition, there’s no prior month to compare against yet.

For real estate agents weighing AI tools, Lofty’s index is a step toward the kind of hard numbers the industry has been missing. It gives them a benchmark to press other vendors on when they make time-saving claims.

However, the most useful measure is their own: tracking whether hours freed up by AI actually turn into more conversations, listings and closings.

Note: Lofty is the official AI partner of Inman.

Proptech companies raised about $1.65 billion across 34 funding rounds in October, according to the Center for Real Estate Technology & Innovation (CRETI), which called it one of the strongest months of 2026.

The money was heavily concentrated. Construction and development took roughly $872.4 million, or 52.8 percent of the total, while residential pulled in $604.4 million, or 36.6 percent. Three deals alone accounted for nearly 75 percent of October capital: Bedrock Robotics’ $600 million Series C, Unlock’s $433.1 million debt financing and ICON’s $200 million Series D.

Debt was a big part of the story. About $588.6 million, more than a third of the month’s total, came through debt rounds. That includes Unlock’s financing for its home-equity agreement platform and CrowdProperty’s roughly $133.5 million round for residential development lending.

That means much of October’s residential funding didn’t go into software at all but into financial products tied to home equity and property lending.

CRETI noted that funding signals investor conviction, not proof of ROI, and said the bar for founders is rising to show a credible link between their technology and a material financial outcome.

The numbers suggest investors are betting less on upcoming real estate agent-facing software and more on the expensive, physical end of housing, such as building homes faster and cheaper and financing the transactions around them.

If that capital pays off, the bigger impact on agents and brokers may come indirectly, through more housing supply and upcoming ways for homeowners to tap equity, rather than through the tools on their desks.

Airbnb looks to roll out its AI travel agent to consumers in the first half of 2027, the firm said in its third-quarter shareholder letter, firming up a timeline it had previously pegged only as sometime in the next year.

Instead of a text-heavy chatbot, the AI agent will assemble a custom interface around each guest’s request, pulling from hundreds of travel-specific components such as maps, photos, comparisons, calendars and itineraries. It will also handle post-booking tasks like reservation changes, refunds, rebooking and payment issues, which Airbnb argues outside AI agents can’t easily do.

CEO Brian Chesky told analysts that general-purpose AI agents are fine for routine tasks but not for trip planning.

“Travel is aspirational,” Chesky said. “Discovering where to go and where to stay is part of the experience.”.

The announcement came alongside a strong third quarter for Airbnb. Revenue grew 19 percent year over year to $4.87 billion, beating Wall Street estimates. Airbnb raised its 2026 growth forecast to the high teens, up from the mid-teens. Chesky called it the tech giant’s fastest revenue growth in more than three years.

Airbnb’s bet is one real estate portals and brokerages are weighing, too: that owning the search experience and the transaction behind it beats handing consumers off to general-purpose AI agents.

If a custom, visual AI agent wins over travelers, it’ll strengthen the case for real estate platforms to build their own AI home-search tools rather than relying on outside chatbots to send them buyers.

RealScout is now showing Zillow Preview listings from hundreds of participating brokerages in its collaborative home search platform, putting pre-MLS inventory in front of buyers searching with their own agents.

The integration, first announced in September, extends Zillow Preview’s reach beyond Zillow, Trulia and Realtor.com to RealScout’s network of more than 100,000 agents.

Preview listings appear in client searches and listing alerts that include Coming Soon properties. Buyers can message their agent directly about a home, and each Preview listing is replaced by its MLS listing once the home goes active. Agents and brokerages don’t need to opt in to see eligible listings.

RealScout CEO Andrew Flachner framed the move as a transparency play, with a not-so-subtle shot at private listing networks.

Industry observers note that “Listing transparency comes down to whether a buyer can choose the agent they trust without worrying that the right home is hiding behind another brokerage’s velvet rope,” Flachner said in a statement. “With Zillow Preview listings from hundreds of brokerages now available in RealScout, agents can give their clients more of the market through the home search experience they already share.”.

In a recent development, for agents, the integration means clients can see pre-MLS listings from participating brokerages in the search tool they already use, without signing up for Zillow or leaving the agent relationship. It also gives buyer’s agents an earlier look at upcoming inventory, which matters most in tight markets, where a few days’ head start can decide who gets a showing first.

Robotics component maker coprod raises $6M to take on robotics ‘integration hell’

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1003 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Robotics component maker coprod Inc.
  • The funding is intended to enable the tech giant to bring its first line of components to market.
  • It works alongside a software application programming interface and a front-end configuration tool to interconnect the components and standardize the communication between them, while preserving the real-time performance required for safe and reliable hardware.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 04:00 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

Robotics component maker coprod Inc. announced today that it has raised $6 million in newly introduced funding to reduce the time and costs associated with building new robotic platforms.

The funding is intended to enable the tech giant to bring its first line of components to market. Founded in 2024, coprod offers an ecosystem of compatible hardware components for robotics and physical artificial intelligence applications.

It works alongside a software application programming interface and a front-end configuration tool to interconnect the components and standardize the communication between them, while preserving the real-time performance required for safe and reliable hardware.

At the core of coprod’s offering is the co:system, which combines the company’s modules on a single real-time EtherCAT control plane with one API in C++ and Python. The product family includes co:power, co:battery, co:sensor and co:motion, with each module able to be used as part of a complete system or integrated on its own.

Coprod is tackling the concern wherein most component suppliers support many protocols in the hope of catering to any integrator, which means their parts rarely work together out of the box. The result, according to coprod, is that building a system from mix-and-match components puts a heavy burden on the integrator. It requires two to three years of custom electronics and software work common before a system is reliable, in a phase known in the industry as “integration hell.”.

The company claims that with its stack, the same work requires only a small team of roboticists, $5,000 to $25,000 per design iteration and a few months of time.

“We believe that a robot with purpose-built hardware designed for a specific task will do that task faster, cheaper and more reliably than any general purpose robot ever could, regardless of which model runs on it,” remarked co-founder and Chief Executive Loïc Delineau.

In a recent development, coming into its fresh funding round, coprod’s components are already powering multiple robots in Switzerland, including the ETH Robotics Club’s XALUN, the first student-built Swiss humanoid robot, which took its first steps in Zurich in recent weeks. The organization is also establishing partnerships with robotics integrators and well-known labs to validate its first hardware prototypes before launching them on the market early next year.

In a recent development, the funding is also intended to support a new hardware prototyping facility in Lausanne. Equipped with CNC lathes, mills, lasers and electronic assembly and testing equipment, the workshop is expected to cut the firm’s development cycles from two weeks to 24 hours. Testing at the site will be used to produce datasheets and digital twin models for each component, an effort aimed at narrowing the gap between simulated and real-world performance that arises in robotics development.

According to recent reports, by the end of 2027, coprod aims to have its entire component line on the market, qualified and certified. Large-scale production is planned for both Shenzhen and Texas, with the company’s headquarters and research and development remaining in Switzerland.

Component supply has also emerged as a constraint for robot makers, particularly in humanoids. A McKinsey & Co. analysis published in April found that supply chain bottlenecks for humanoids are most likely to emerge around actuators and sensing and perception systems, the type of hardware coprod is developing.

It has been revealed that delineau formed coprod with Chief Technology Officer Vincent Nguyen and Chief Scientist Matthias Schuller (pictured), all graduates of the École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne. The three started out by building a bipedal robot demonstrator in a parent’s garage in the Swiss Alps to show what compatible components could do.

According to recent reports, founderful AG and Prototype Capital led the pre-seed round, with General Catalyst Group Management, Pace Ventures, Tiny Supercomputer Investment Company, Kima Ventures, SDAC, Unruly Capital and Venture Kick also participating. Angel investors in the round include Hugging Face Inc. co-founder Thomas Wolf, the Dassault family and Florent Perrichon. Venture Kick awarded coprod CHF 40,000 ($47,600) earlier this year.

Andreas Klinger, founder of Prototype, stated coprod is fixing “the biggest problem in hardware.” It argues that robotics founders need a single standard for basic components and middleware so they can focus on the parts of their products that create value for customers.

The crypto market has endured heavy liquidations and risk-off selling, while money rotates toward AI stocks and other opportunities.

In a recent development, that reading comes as sentiment across crypto has turned deeply pessimistic. Tech Report: Existing-home sales sink to a 16-year low as mortgage rates bite

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • October was the perfect storm for existing-home sales, with a typical seasonal slowdown made worse by elevated mortgage rates, a worsening macroeconomic environment and political uncertainty.
  • Existing-home sales during October declined 5.5 percent month-over-month and 8.8 percent year-over-year to a seasonally adjusted rate of 3.75 million, the lowest rate since August 2010 (3.68 million).
  • Despite slowing sales, unsold inventory (1.59 million units) and the median home price ($416,700) increased by 1.3 percent and 0.4 percent, respectively.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

October was the perfect storm for existing-home sales, with a typical seasonal slowdown made worse by elevated mortgage rates, a worsening macroeconomic environment and political uncertainty.

Existing-home sales during October declined 5.5 percent month-over-month and 8.8 percent year-over-year to a seasonally adjusted rate of 3.75 million, the lowest rate since August 2010 (3.68 million). Annual sales declined in all four regions; however, the Northeast was the only region to also experience a month-over-month drop.

Despite slowing sales, unsold inventory (1.59 million units) and the median home price ($416,700) increased by 1.3 percent and 0.4 percent, respectively.

NAR Chief Economist Lawrence Yun noted mortgage rates are the primary cause of current market woes.

According to recent reports, fixed rates experienced a rapid-fire ascent at the beginning of the fall, breaching 7 percent on Sept. 24 and then roughly a week later reaching a three-year high of 7.40 percent on Oct. 8. The catalyst had been two-fold: the Federal Reserve had hiked the federal funds rate (i.e., short-term rate) by 25 basis points during its Sept. 16 FOMC meeting and 10-year Treasury yields were rising at a historic pace.

Rates have since relaxed to the lower 7 percent range, but the short-term damage is already done.

“Homebuying is difficult when mortgage rates have climbed to their highest levels since 2000, aside from a single month in 2023,” Yun said in a written statement. “As a result, home sales fell to their lowest level since August 2010.”.

Although Freddie Mac’s Primary Mortgage Market Survey saw rates drop for the fourth consecutive week to 7.11 percent, Bright MLS Chief Economist Lisa Sturtevant mentioned she expects mortgage rates to start rising again in the coming weeks because of sticky inflation.

According to recent reports, “There is little reason to expect rates to come down before the end of the year,” Sturtevant said in an emailed statement. “In fact, given this week’s inflation report, it is much more likely for us to see rates increase instead of decrease.”.

Yun and Sturtevant remarked mortgage rates will continue to impact home sales — not inventory and home price growth.

Sources indicate that “So far, we haven’t seen higher rates lead to widespread price declines. In fact, home prices are still rising in many local markets,” Sturtevant said. “Inventory is rising, but higher rates are holding back some sellers along with buyers. Because both sides of the supply-demand equation are slowing, it’s not likely for home prices to drop significantly, even if rates move higher.”.

Recent findings suggest that added Yun, “It will be the highest inventory count since November 2019. We are now back to pre-COVID inventory conditions.”.

Mortgage rate volatility has pushed homebuyers to slow down or pull out of the market altogether, as shown by September’s pending home sales, which declined 7.3 percent month over month and 11.3 percent year over year.

Sources indicate that as a result, homes are sitting on the market longer, averaging 35 days. Most homesellers, Yun said, can wait for the market to turn in their favor, thanks to strong home price appreciation.

“Despite fewer transactions in October, the 88 million homeowners across the country are largely in a comfortable financial position due to sizable housing wealth accumulation,” he stated. “The number of distressed property sales remains historically low at only 2 percent of all transactions.”.

However, if a homeseller is in the position where they have to sell now, due to career or family changes, they’ll need to get comfortable with making a price cut.

“If the homes are not selling at the listing price, it requires a discount,” Yun remarked in a pre-report call Thursday morning. “The longer the days on market, the larger the discount. If the home is sitting on the market for more than 60 days, it requires a 9 percent discount … Even with this discount that is occurring, the median home price is still squeaking out a small gain.”.

Yun and Realtor.com Chief Economist Danielle Hale said existing-home sales could improve in November and December — if mortgage rates continue to relax.

“Fortunately, the 10-year Treasury yield has pulled back from its early October highs, which has helped nudge mortgage rates below this recent peak,” she noted. “However, several factors are likely to put a floor under how low rates can go.”.

Hale said jobs and inflation trends will determine whether rates can move back toward the high sixes.

“[The] expected need for tighter monetary policy in the near term combined with sizable demand for capital from both governments and private companies, largely to finance AI-related investments [also matter],” she noted. “Put simply, I expect to see more homebuyers come back into the market as we move away from recent mortgage rate highs, but the upside will be limited.”.

Yun mentioned rates below 7 percent could unleash a wave of untapped demand, allowing homebuyers to finally seize the advantage they’ve been given in terms of income growth, inventory and negotiating power.

“One wonders whether current price-declining markets will see buyers step in and stabilize the market,” he stated. “We are not in a recession, and we are adding jobs. First part is prices, second is income growth. Wage growth is helping modestly on home affordability, but the substantial change is from mortgage rates. If mortgage rates can come down under 7 percent, we’ll see whether we see more buyer traffic.”.

Sources indicate that however, Sturtevant is less bullish on mortgage rates, noting that rate shifts don’t guarantee buyers the affordability break they seek. The Bright MLS economist pointed to the fact that home prices have continued rising in many markets, despite rates exceeding 7 percent.

“There is little reason to expect rates to come down further this year,” she noted. “In fact, given this week’s inflation report, it is much more likely for us to see rates increase instead of decrease. Data on fresh pending contracts, showing activity and buyer traffic suggest that sales are going to continue to be anemic in the 4th quarter. It is very likely we will end 2026 with a total of fewer than 4 million existing home sales for the first time since the 1990s.”.

Jennifer Garner is getting a head start on Christmas at her Los Angeles home, where thousands of lights are already twinkling and monogrammed stockings hang above the fireplace.

The 54-year-old actress shared a look at her holiday decorations on Instagram, revealing that even her greenhouse got a festive touch with a wreath of its own.

Thanksgiving preparations were underway in the kitchen, where Garner gave the turkey a trial run ahead of the big day. Her dogs and cat were dressed for the occasion, too, in turkey costumes.

“We’re ready over here,” Garner wrote in the caption.

Recent findings suggest that garner has been known to love the holiday season, having previously opened up about her favorite memories during a Nov. 4 episode of the "Happy Hour With Ina Garten" podcast.

“My favorite Thanksgivings were when my kids were really little, I think it was right at the end of 'Alias,' and it was at a significant house,” said Garner, who shares Violet, 20, Seraphina, 17, and Samuel, 14, with her ex-husband Ben Affleck.

According to recent reports, “My kids were little, and Ben and I were there, and we all cooked. Bradley made the stuffing and Victor made ... I think Victor’s sister came. It was just our little 'Alias' family cooking together. It was so special," she added, referring to her co-stars Victor Garber, Ron Rifkin, and Bradley Cooper.

Despite separating in 2015 and divorcing in 2018, Garner and Affleck have continued to celebrate the holidays together.

Last year, a source told People that the couple spent the holidays together in Los Angeles.

“Jen makes it very special. She’s such a great chef. She loves having her whole family together, too. Ben’s always welcome at her house,” the source told the outlet.

Garner is known for showing off touching memories at her dwelling.

Last year, Garner and her mom were brought to tears when they were surprised with a near-perfect re-creation of the kitchen that sat inside the actress' childhood home in West Virginia.

Garner and her mom, Patricia Ann, couldn't help but get emotional when they were brought to the space, which had been designed by appliance firm KitchenAid to perfectly mirror the kitchen of their Charleston, WV, home.

The mother-daughter duo initially thought they were being brought in to take part in a holiday photo shoot, but after stepping inside the kitchen set, which looked identical to the one in their Greystone Place abode, they were left gobsmacked.

Both Garner and her mom began welling up at seeing their vintage wooden table and green refrigerator, with both women rapidly recalling the happy memories they had made in the original space.

It has been revealed that “This is where we would hang out, all our crafts happened right here with somebody looking through from that side," Garner mentioned, while looking through the cupboards. "This is the cabinet where you hid the chocolate chips.".

The kitchen boasted a large wooden table, matching wooden cabinets, yellow oven, granite countertops, drawings, and a yellow KitchenAid mixer.

Industry observers note that the "13 Going on 30" star then pointed at a nostalgic photo of her mom that was placed on the counter. It reminded her of the days that Patricia would get her perm done while "sitting at the table.".

“It’s a privilege to get to see where we used to be. I want that to be the den, and then I want to hear dad come home from work. That’s what I feel," Patricia said.

The 87-year-old noted that the patterned wallpaper in the replica kitchen first caught her eye.

Garner noted that the experience gave her a "really deep feeling of homesickness and gratitude.".

Patricia previously joined her daughter on Garner's latest installment of her "Pretend Cooking Show.".

Binance will delist GAS/TRY, HBAR/BNB, HIVE/TRY, KSM/TRY and ZAMA/TRY pairs on November 20, 2026 at 03:00 UTC, according to an official announcement published on November 18.

The exchange clarified that people will still be able to trade the affected tokens through other available spot trading pairs on its platform.

Sources indicate that in related news, Binance Margin will initiate a routine cleanup of Cross Margin accounts with collateral valued at less than 1 USD (or equivalent in other assets), effective from November 30, 2026 at 00:00 (UTC). The cleanup will be executed on a daily basis as an ongoing operational process.

Affected accounts include Cross Margin Accounts with a collateral value of less than 1 USD equivalent across all assets and no outstanding liabilities, as well as Margin Accounts with no capital activity in the past 6 months. Capital activity refers to any action that generates a capital flow.

For each eligible Small-Asset Account, the system will automatically transfer the collateral in owners’ Margin Accounts to their Spot Accounts while the Margin Account functions remain normal, allowing users to transfer, borrow, or trade at any time after the cleanup.

Accounts with collateral equal to or exceeding 1 USD equivalent are not affected by this cleanup.

What do door-to-door Bible salesmen have to do with luxury real estate? For Wade Shealy, everything.

Recent findings suggest that on this episode of Real Estate Insiders Unfiltered, James Dwiggins and Keith Robinson sit down with Shealy, founder and CEO of ThirdHome, the luxury home exchange club he started in 2010 with just two homes. Today it has more than 35,000 homes in over 100 countries. Shealy shares how selling Bibles and dictionaries door to door paid his way through the University of Georgia and how it led him to Hilton Head in 1984 to a career in resort real estate.

Sources indicate that he explains why second homeowners kept coming back within five years wanting to sell and how that pattern became the idea for ThirdHome. He also walks through how he signed up his first 1,500 members and how the club’s key system works. Plus, he shares the biggest lesson he’s learned from his partner, Mrs. Fields founder Debbi Fields: Make everyone you meet feel important.

They also get into handling rejection, taking major risks and why Shealy believes very few people will buy a vacation home without a home exchange membership 10 years from now.

Shealy explains the luxury home exchange club model simply. Owners deposit unused weeks in their second home and earn credits called keys. They use those keys to book stays in other members’ homes, paying only an exchange fee of around $900 instead of thousands in rent. The club has now completed 100,000 exchanges, and Shealy states many members who would never rent out their home happily exchange it.

Recent findings suggest that for agents, Shealy points to ThirdHome’s ambassador program. In Cabo San Lucas, developers began offering ThirdHome access as part of their sales pitch, and the club grew to roughly 8,000 properties there. He believes the next generation of buyers will expect mobility and experiences, not just a single vacation home.

His advice for agents: Look at what everyone else is doing, and do the opposite. Above all, keep changing, because if you’re marketing the same way you did 20 years ago, you’re already behind.

Sources indicate that post-quantum cryptography startup Q Security Inc. formally launched today with $11.5 million in upcoming funding for a platform designed to take enterprises from discovery through to completion of their quantum-safe migrations.

Founded this year, Q.security offers a remediation platform that runs the move to post-quantum cryptography as one coordinated program. The tech giant argues that security teams need business context to decide which cryptographic findings to address first, since the time and resources available for the work are limited.

At the core of the Q.security offering is a map of an organization’s business structure and applications. Findings from the cryptographic inventory are tied back to that map, with the highest-risk assets put at the front of the queue.

In a recent development, teams are mentioned to be able to investigate exposure and work through remediation using a conversational artificial intelligence interface. Through integrations with existing cybersecurity and infrastructure tools, the platform drives fixes to completion using AI-guided runbooks, ticketing and automation.

Sources indicate that once a fix is in place, Q.security verifies that it works. Monitoring of the organization’s cryptographic posture then continues as standards and threats change, an approach the organization claims lets security teams reduce risk faster and at lower cost.

“Quantum computing is making cryptographic risk an urgent and ongoing business priority,” said Guy Peer, co-founder and chief executive of Q.security, who previously co-founded Unbound Security and led its research and development through its acquisition by Coinbase Global Inc., declared in 2021.

Industry observers note that peer’s co-founder, Nir Steinherz, was director of product at Coinbase and vice president of strategy and product at Unbound Security. He was also a senior vice president at Citigroup Inc.’s Security Innovation Center, where he led secure digital banking initiatives for more than 100 million customers. The pair are said to have led a cryptographic migration protecting hundreds of billions of dollars in assets.

The funding is intended to support Q.security as it brings its platform to enterprise customers through direct sales and channel partners.

Castle Island Ventures led the seed round, with Upcoming York Life Ventures, Coinbase Ventures, Fin Capital, SBI US Gateway Fund and Ground Up Ventures also participating.

Matt Walsh, general partner at Castle Island Ventures, said enterprises know they need to prepare for the day quantum computers can break current encryption. With harvest-now, decrypt-later data collection already under way, “the challenge is determining how to prioritize the migration across business and technology environments,” he added.

The rise of the multi-market agent: Why local expertise is going global

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (763 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that wealth is mobile, and so are luxury clients.
  • It has been revealed that ask a luxury client where they live, and the answer is increasingly more than one place.
  • Sources indicate that wealth has become more mobile, and so have the people who hold it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that wealth is mobile, and so are luxury clients. Here’s how the multi-market real estate agent combines local expertise with a connected brokerage network.

It has been revealed that ask a luxury client where they live, and the answer is increasingly more than one place. A primary home in Los Angeles, a ski house in Aspen, a pied-à-terre in New York, a winter retreat in Miami or the Caribbean.

Sources indicate that wealth has become more mobile, and so have the people who hold it. The agents who serve these clients best are evolving alongside them, building expertise across markets and cultivating relationships that extend well beyond their own backyards.

That shift is changing what it means to be a local expert. For brokerage leaders, it also raises an notable question: Are we building networks that reflect how our clients actually live?

Remote work, flexible schedules and a generation of buyers who think of themselves as global citizens have loosened the link between where someone earns, where they live and where they invest.

Today’s luxury buyers are driven by lifestyle, whether that means access to mountains, water, a particular school system or a city’s cultural calendar, and they are comfortable buying in places where they spend only part of the year. What has not changed is their expectation of personalized service.

For these clients, a traditional handoff creates friction. Each time they are passed from one agent to another, they repeat their goals, rebuild trust and wonder whether anyone sees the full picture. A client’s real estate portfolio is one story. Their advisor should be able to tell it across markets.

In a recent development, going global does not mean going generic. A Manhattan co-op board, a Florida insurance requirement, a Colorado water right and a California disclosure obligation each carry real consequences, and clients need professionals who understand the market in which they are buying or selling.

The mistake is confusing geographic reach with geographic expertise. The strongest multi-market agents know where their knowledge is deepest and where collaboration adds value. The future of the multi-market real estate agent isn’t about being an expert everywhere. It’s about knowing where your expertise ends, who to bring into the conversation and how to make that collaboration seamless for the client.

Recent findings suggest that when a client has a positive experience with an agent in one city, that relationship shouldn’t end at the city limits. But there is a meaningful difference between providing a referral and extending a trusted relationship. If an agent simply passes along a name, the client starts over. If that introduction comes with shared context and a clear understanding of the client’s priorities, the experience feels seamless.

Trust is portable, but only when it is supported by consistent service and relationships built before a client needs them.

Recent findings suggest that A global footprint alone does not create a global client experience. Offices in multiple markets mean little if they operate independently. Brokerages need to provide the infrastructure that makes cross-market relationships work, including introductions between offices, shared market intelligence, consistent training and clear expectations around communication and referrals.

At The Agency, we encourage agents to bring colleagues from other offices into client relationships early, so clients experience a connected team rather than a series of separate introductions. Technology helps agents share insights, access inventory and present properties remotely, but the real advantage comes from the relationships behind it.

Start by looking at the markets that consistently appear in your referral activity and client conversations. Those patterns show where to build stronger partnerships between offices.

Sources indicate that invest in cross-market education so agents recognize regional nuances and regulatory considerations and know when to bring in specialized expertise. Set clear collaboration standards for how clients are introduced, who takes the lead and how agents stay involved. Then measure success beyond the transaction: Did the client feel supported, and was communication consistent?

Industry observers note that as brokerage leaders, we should be asking whether our networks are simply growing in size or becoming more connected. Those are very different measures of success.

Local expertise has never been more valuable. What is changing is its reach. The brokerages that treat their agents’ knowledge as a connected network, rather than a set of separate territories, will be better positioned to serve today’s clients and the next generation of buyers who increasingly see the world, not one city, as their real estate market.

Rainy Hake Austin is president of The Agency in Los Angeles. Get connected on Instagram.

Although XRP is at risk of losing its top-four position in the global cryptocurrency market, the asset still ranks among the three largest crypto assets in Japan.

In a recent post shared by the renowned Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm Evernorth, the firm highlighted XRP’s growing performance in the Japan crypto market.

Earlier today, Evernorth shared monthly data from the Japan Virtual and Crypto Assets Exchange Association (JVCEA) revealing that XRP recorded about ¥132.8 billion in spot trading volume in September 2026.

While this accounted for about 15% of Japan's total crypto spot trading volume during the month, XRP emerged as the third most-traded cryptocurrency in Japan after Bitcoin and Ethereum.

This demonstrates that XRP has outperformed other major altcoins that are at the moment trading in the Japan crypto market, hitting about $880 million in trading volume.

While further data indicated Solana and Dogecoin ranking next to XRP on the list as the fourth- and fifth-largest cryptocurrencies in Japan, respectively, the data also showed a wide gap from XRP’s ¥132.8 billion spot volume.

This means that XRP is significantly ahead of Solana and Dogecoin in the Japan crypto trading market, as Solana recorded only about ¥19.47 billion in trading volume during the same month.

Dogecoin, on the other hand, saw less participation, as it recorded only ¥11.27 billion in spot volume during the same period.

With XRP sitting in the third spot, the asset has become one of the most actively traded cryptocurrencies in Japan despite its persistent price volatility.

A trip to California had been a possibility, but the Duke and Duchess of Sussex intend to spend both Thanksgiving and Christmas in Britain after six years on the West Coast.

“Maybe gumbo, yeah, maybe turkey, maybe gumbo,” he noted.

Industry observers note that “Everything going on with her dad is still weighing heavily on her,” a source told People. “She wants the holidays to be as quiet and enjoyable as possible for the family.

“Traveling back and forth would be too much for everyone,” the source added.

Since Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, returned to school, Meghan and Harry have been making more time for meals out together.

Beyond their education, Harry said returning to Britain has allowed his children to spend more time with relatives and develop closer relationships with family friends.

In a recent development, another motivation for the move, he explained, was to “be back closer to my family and to be back on U.K. soil for longer than a few days or a week here or there.

“It’s been nice to be close to friends, family, friends and friends and their children as well, to be able to have endless playdates to really, like, help our kids settle in," he noted.

Despite the significance of the relocation, Harry admitted that he and Meghan had not necessarily mapped out the move years in advance.

Bootstrapped startup Levenza brings consumer-style personal agents to business workers
