What music sells a house? Agents say it’s not about genre

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1536 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, taylor Swift, classical or silence?
  • Recent findings suggest that ask real estate agents what soundtrack sells a house, and you’ll get two answers.
  • Inman asked agents and brokers from Manhattan to Breckenridge, Colorado, and they described the music they play at showings and open houses and how they match it to the property.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, taylor Swift, classical or silence? Agents explain how they pick open house music, the one rule most follow and why none can prove it works.

Recent findings suggest that ask real estate agents what soundtrack sells a house, and you’ll get two answers. One is a carefully curated playlist, while the other is silence.

Inman asked agents and brokers from Manhattan to Breckenridge, Colorado, and they described the music they play at showings and open houses and how they match it to the property.

Industry observers note that none could point to hard numbers showing a playlist moved a home faster or for more money. What they did offer was a clear set of rules from the agents who use music, and an equally firm argument from those who won’t touch it.

Ben Jacobs, co-founder of the Chestler Jacobs Team at Douglas Elliman in New York City, thinks music raises more questions than it answers. He remarked he’s not a fan of playing music during showings.

According to recent reports, “Buyers may wonder if the agent is trying to mask something, whether it’s street noise, construction nearby, sounds within the building or even a noisy appliance,” Jacobs told Inman. “You want buyers to experience the home as it actually is, without anything distracting from their ability to evaluate the space.”.

Sources indicate that his co-founder, Jessica Chestler, said music has its place. That place is just not a private showing.

“Music can be wonderful for setting a mood at a cocktail party, listing launch or special event, but during a showing, I think there’s something to be said for letting the property speak for itself,” Chestler said.

Megan Sullivan works at the same brokerage, and she uses music for the very reason Jacobs avoids it. Sullivan sells large estate homes across Fairfield and Westchester counties out of Douglas Elliman’s Greenwich, Connecticut, office. Some of those homes sit within earshot of things a seller can’t fix.

“I actually do like incorporating music into certain showings, particularly when a property is impacted by outside noise from planes, trains or automobiles,” Sullivan said. “Thoughtfully selected background music can help create a more welcoming atmosphere and soften those distractions, allowing buyers to focus on the overall experience of the home. I think it’s very property-specific.”.

Industry observers note that jeffrey Hensel is a broker associate with North Coast Financial, a California hard money lender that funds fix-and-flip and probate deals. He looks at it from the investor side.

It has been revealed that “Dead silence can amplify every creak, clank, and drip in an otherwise quiet home,” he stated. “Background music masks these sounds and provides some white noise to help set a calm mood.”.

Agents in the pro-music camp mostly aren’t trying to cover anything up. They simply want buyers to stay longer.

In a recent development, sandra Daniels of Harry Norman, Realtors | Forbes Global Properties serves the East Cobb and Marietta area outside Atlanta. She’s currently listing a $3.9 million estate in The River Club in Suwanee, Georgia.

For those showings, she rotates light classical piano, The Macarons Project and a Spotify playlist called “Nora Ephron + Nancy Meyers Dinner Party.”.

“Put a buyer in a home with a glass of Champagne or a cup of coffee and the right music playing, and that cozy, inviting atmosphere encourages people to stay, relax and feel at home,” Daniels told Inman.

It has been revealed that daniels also has a low-tech trick for vacant listings she expects to sell in the first week. She bought an old-school CD player and a few classical CDs. She leaves it on repeat through the first weekend of showings and stops by each evening to turn off the lights and music and lock up.

Recent findings suggest that natalia Bassova, founder and CEO of Resort Real Estate in Breckenridge, Colorado, saw the same effect at a luxury mountain listing. The home looked great, she noted, but it highlighted cold.

“By adding some background instrumental music, it gave the buyers more time to spend in the home. They spent more time in the kitchen and great room areas,” Bassova said. “The property didn’t change, but the atmosphere did.”.

Industry observers note that for mountain and luxury homes, Bassova plays acoustic and piano music, including Ludovico Einaudi and The Piano Guys. For condos and fresh construction, she switches to soft contemporary instrumentals.

Agents who play music disagree on genre, but almost all agree on one thing: avoid lyrics.

Sources indicate that “If the buyer begins to think about the music, then it is having a negative impact,” Bassova said. Her never-play list covers anything with strong lyrics, politics, swearing or heavy bass.

Andrea Seeney is a global real estate advisor with Atlanta Fine Homes Sotheby’s International Realty and a trained opera singer and classical pianist. She compared lyrics to a seller’s personal effects.

“Acoustic performances are best because they set a tone and allow the buyer to fill in the blanks with their own thoughts,” Seeney said.

She leans toward jazz and usually plays Spotify’s Coffee House radio or its Ella Fitzgerald playlist. She says music works on buyers through memory: a song can take someone back to a time and place they enjoyed, “and that memory then reflects positively on the home.”.

According to recent reports, hensel takes the lyrics rule a step further, to genre itself. If an agent plays hip-hop or country for a buyer who doesn’t listen to it, he claims, that signals an assumption about who the buyer is. That can create friction neither side notices. His pick is quiet cocktail-lounge jazz like Miles Davis or Bill Evans, at a steady tempo and volume.

In a recent development, he also cited retail research by psychological scientists Adrian North and Lorraine Sheridan of Curtin University and Charles Areni of Macquarie University. It found that shoppers who heard classical music rated merchandise as higher quality and were willing to spend more.

Some agents ignore the rulebook completely.

Rachel Kilmer, an agent with ReeceNichols Real Estate in Kansas City, Missouri, plays Taylor Swift at nearly every open house. She swaps in country for more rural listings.

According to recent reports, “In Kansas City, she’s a conversation starter,” Kilmer mentioned. “People come in, and it’s, ‘Are you a Swiftie?’ ‘No, but I love the Chiefs!’ It really helps loosen up the conversation.”.

She added, “I’m the one sitting there listening to it for two hours!”.

Monica Shea, a broker with KW Aspire in Colorado Springs, Colorado, builds whole open houses around a theme, and the music follows.

Recent findings suggest that she played the Eras Tour set list at a Taylor Swift–themed open house and the Frozen soundtrack at a hot cocoa bar event. A Halloween open house got not-too-spooky Halloween music. For regular showings, she has sellers put on a YouTube channel with seasonal background music and scenery.

Shea’s never-play list puts her directly at odds with a few other agents: smooth jazz. Shea says she never plays “anything that sounds like the Weather Channel.”.

Marcel Finkelstein of Team BlackStar at eXp Realty hosts open houses every Sunday across Monmouth County, New Jersey. He sees music as more of an icebreaker than a staging tool.

Industry observers note that his Apple Music rotation includes lounge instrumentals, vocal-free dance-pop and Bon Entendeur. It also has Afro house from DJ Alex Niyazov and the warm trumpet and sax of Fausto Papetti and Paul Mauriat.

He uses the same approach whether the listing is a $600,000 two-bedroom condo in Manalapan or a $2 million six-bedroom in Colts Neck.

“I want the atmosphere to feel calm, comfortable and welcoming, rather than like a sales presentation,” Finkelstein said.

Finkelstein added that his Instagram followers also know how much he loves music.

“Every week, I share newly introduced songs and incorporate music into my stories and posts about homes,” he said. “It’s a personal interest that carries through into how I present properties.”.

Recent findings suggest that on setup, agents who play music give similar advice. Keep the volume low enough that buyers can ask questions and the agent can hear their feedback. Use one good speaker rather than several.

Recent findings suggest that bassova puts hers in the middle of the home, and Seeney puts a small Bluetooth speaker in the kitchen. When sellers have a Sonos system, Daniels connects to it from her MacBook or iPad. Otherwise, she brings her own Bose speaker.

According to recent reports, kilmer runs her music from an iPad instead of her phone. “That way, incoming calls and texts don’t interrupt the music,” she said.

Industry observers note that as for proof, none of the agents Inman spoke with track music as a performance metric. Bassova stated she gets buyer feedback that certain homes feel relaxing, but nothing tied to days on market or offers.

So the evidence is anecdotal, and the playlists don’t agree. Agents can’t even settle on jazz. Both camps share one goal: the buyer should notice the home, not the soundtrack.

As Bassova said, “If the buyer begins to think about the music, then it is having a negative impact.”.

#167791. CrowdStrike’s Zscaler deal is a $44B vote for platformization and a long-term threat to Palo Alto Networks

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2020 w)

CrowdStrike’s Zscaler deal is a $44B vote for platformization and a long-term threat to Palo Alto Networks

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2020 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For decades, the security industry has told buyers to choose best-of-breed security products, leaving practitioners to stitch them together.
  • This has been perpetuated by the major analyst firms, which have a Wave for this product and a Magic Quadrant for that product.
  • has long articulated the value of security platformization.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:11 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

ANALYSIS by Zeus Kerravala.

For decades, the security industry has told buyers to choose best-of-breed security products, leaving practitioners to stitch them together.

This has been perpetuated by the major analyst firms, which have a Wave for this product and a Magic Quadrant for that product. The reality is that choosing best-of-breed everywhere has never led to best-in-class threat protection.

Palo Alto Networks Inc. has long articulated the value of security platformization. To be precise, Fortinet Inc. was the first vendor to advance the concept of a security platform, but no security provider has pushed the industry as hard as Palo Alto. Chief Executice Nikesh Arora has been vocal about platforms as the only way to truly protect the entire attack surface.

Industry observers note that crowdStrike Holdings Inc.’s agreement to acquire Zscaler Inc. for $43.9 billion strongly supports the thesis. SiliconANGLE has been covering the deal, so I won’t rehash the details. In short, the leader in endpoint security is buying the leader in cloud-delivered zero-trust access. The combined firm is expected to start with more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue, and the deal is expected to close between August 2027 and January 2028.

Over the long term, the combination poses a real threat to Palo Alto. In the short term, it is a strong co-sell opportunity for CrowdStrike and Zscaler, with significant integration work between the two.

Industry observers note that arora has long argued that customers want fewer vendors and integrated platforms. Getting there can be challenging, as security teams often operate with an “if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it” mentality. The mere thought of replacing a working product is enough to keep even the most seasoned security pros up at night. In February 2024, when he cut guidance to fund the platform push, Palo Alto’s stock fell 28% in a day. Since then, the stock has recovered nicely, validating his strategy, and its rival has now raised $44 billion to head down its own platform journey.

Sources indicate that in some ways, CrowdStrike and Zscaler were the strongest argument against platformization, though one could argue that each was its own smaller “platform,” depending on how you define it. Each led its category, and the two were close partners, with more than 2,000 shared customers and 16 product integrations. If best-of-breed products, tied together by integrations, could work anywhere, it was here. The two companies are now taking it a step further. “When you integrate as partners, there’s only so much you can do,” Zscaler founder and CEO Jay Chaudhry remarked on the analyst call.

The “why now?” question is worth asking, as the coming together of these two companies has been rumored for some time. The answer is that agentic AI creates latest challenges and risks that are difficult to address through a partnership. An AI agent runs on a device and then crosses the network to access models, tools, and data, operating at machine speed around the clock. A vendor that sees only the device or only the network sees only half of what the agent does. CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said adversaries are “exploiting the seams and the gaps between companies’ integrations.”.

Recent findings suggest that I agree. Every seam between products is a place for an attacker to hide, and AI-driven attacks exploit those seams faster than security teams can close them. But a platform is more than one vendor and one contract. It means one dataset, one agent, and one policy engine, so a detection on a laptop triggers enforcement across the network without a person in the middle. If that’s the standard, CrowdStrike, while it currently describes itself as a platform, is not today.

According to recent reports, with Zscaler, CrowdStrike is more than just a product to fill a gap. Zscaler is a best-in-class Secure Access Service Edge stack that protects half of the Fortune 500 and runs what it calls the world’s largest inline security cloud.

Recent findings suggest that it is also built for resilience, which matters more than ever. Last week, I wrote about six major outages over six days at organizations ranging from Microsoft to the Federal Aviation Administration. Zscaler sits between every user and every application, so if it fails, the business stops. That has forced the company to engineer for failure.

Its Business Continuity Cloud provides each customer with a dedicated backup environment in third-party data centers, on separate networks and DNS, with software updates deliberately staggered so a bad release can’t affect both simultaneously. “No linkage — no network, no shared routers, no switches, no shared network operations,” Chaudhry told me in a previous conversation.

Of all companies, CrowdStrike should value that. In July 2024, a faulty Falcon patch affected an estimated 8.5 million Windows devices. The standard objection to platformization is concentration risk, and it intensifies when a single vendor controls both the endpoint agent and the path to every application. Zscaler’s continuity design is the best answer to that objection I’ve seen, and CrowdStrike should extend it across Falcon.

The near-term value is commercial. CrowdStrike notes about 8,000 Zscaler customers don’t yet buy from it. Channel partners already sell both companies, and the two sales teams already work deals together.

After the close, Zscaler will transition to Falcon Flex, CrowdStrike’s licensing model. “A Zscaler customer can add Falcon. A Falcon customer can add Zscaler. One contract, one platform,” Kurtz said. CrowdStrike expects about $1 billion in annualized revenue synergies within 30 months of closing.

This target seems bullish but achievable, as it requires no code integration — only sales execution, which both companies are good at.

Sources indicate that today, the Falcon sensor and Zscaler’s client run as separate agents on separate clouds with different release schedules. Kurtz promised that it will collapse into one. “The brand promise, single agent, that’s not going to change,” he remarked. CrowdStrike’s next-generation sensor can already inspect and proxy network traffic, he added, which should make the job easier.

Sources indicate that kurtz was also candid about the effort: “Yes, there’s hard work to be done. There always is in an acquisition.” CrowdStrike gave no timeline. The engineering teams can’t combine until the deal closes, which is at least eight months away. CrowdStrike’s largest prior acquisition cost less than $1 billion. Folding Zscaler’s global security cloud into Falcon is far harder than anything it has attempted. Until that work is done, the platform exists on slides.

In a recent development, that gap gives Palo Alto time to further its own platform. It closed its CyberArk acquisition in February, renamed the business Idira, and is already cross-selling it to its existing customers.

Industry observers note that the long term looks different. If CrowdStrike delivers a single agent and a single dataset, Palo Alto will face something it hasn’t had: a rival of similar scale with the leading endpoint product and the leading zero-trust cloud on one platform. Palo Alto is most exposed in SASE, where its Prisma SASE business has been chasing Zscaler.

CrowdStrike plus Zscaler make a formidable platform, but it still lacks a firewall. Zscaler is a cloud proxy, and many enterprises that use it still run firewalls in their data centers, campuses, and clouds. That is Palo Alto’s core area of strength.

Industry observers note that looking ahead, that should open the door to another acquisition. Check Point is the obvious choice, as it will struggle over the long term as a firewall pure-play in a market shifting to platforms, and it would give CrowdStrike a large installed base. If CrowdStrike wants a broader networking portfolio, Fortinet is the bigger swing, with switching, wireless and software-defined wide-area network alongside its firewalls. The two already partner on endpoint and firewall protection.

In a recent development, either deal would add more integration work to Zscaler, so I wouldn’t expect either to happen soon. But a tech giant that wants to displace Palo Alto can’t leave the firewall to someone else forever. I understand zero trust can replace a number of firewalls, particularly in branch offices, but firewalls are here to stay for the foreseeable future.

In a recent development, the deal also puts smaller security vendors in play. Netskope and Cato Networks are both independent SASE vendors competing against a bundle, and Oppenheimer has already named Netskope an attractive target.

Fortinet is an obvious acquirer, but the buyer pool extends beyond security companies. Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co., following its acquisition of Juniper Networks Inc., is embedding security across its network and may seek to bolster that portfolio. Dell Technologies Inc. lags in security, with a portfolio centered on data protection and resilience, and could benefit from an acquisition to close the gap.

Nothing changes today, and customers shouldn’t pause their projects. I’d use the waiting period to prepare in advance.

Buy what is integrated. Ask for the integration roadmap with dates for the single agent, the shared data set and unified policy. Until those ship, evaluate CrowdStrike and Zscaler as two products.

Use leverage. Palo Alto is trying to pry Zscaler accounts loose, and CrowdStrike and Zscaler want commitments before the close. As Sanchit Vir Gogia of Greyhound Research told CSO, “Consolidation is sold at the first signature and priced at the second.” Negotiate price caps for renewals now.

Industry observers note that get interoperability in writing. When asked about lock-in, Kurtz remarked, “We have and will continue to work well with all of the other technologies and ecosystem.” If you run Zscaler with another endpoint product or Falcon with another access provider, include that promise in your contract.

It has been revealed that make resilience a requirement. Ask CrowdStrike to commit to maintaining Zscaler’s Business Continuity Cloud and its staggered updates, and to apply the same discipline to a combined agent.

Industry observers note that this deal settles the argument over platformization. Who wins is still unclear. CrowdStrike has to do the integration work, and Palo Alto has the better part of a year to persuade customers not to wait. The great news for customers is that big moves like this create a wave of innovation. AI is changing security faster than ever before, and a CrowdStrike-vs.-Palo Alto battle is good for everyone.

Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BlackRock, the leading asset management firm and Bitcoin’s largest ETF issuer, sparked discussions earlier today following a massive Bitcoin sale by the company.

The latest data showcased by SosoValue shows that the leading Bitcoin fund has witnessed massive single-day withdrawals from investors who have ventured into its Bitcoin investment product.

Earlier today, BlackRock sold over half a billion dollars’ worth of Bitcoin after its spot Bitcoin ETF, also known as iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), recorded a total of $541.08 million in net outflows.

This massive outflow has come as Bitcoin’s price decline continues to intensify, causing investors to aggressively pull their money out of the fund amid growing market fear.

While this marks the third time this week that BlackRock has recorded a net outflow amid persistent market volatility, it also marks the largest single-day outflow BlackRock has recorded since its launch.

Apparently, the record-breaking withdrawal that the fund just witnessed suggests that institutional and traditional investors are becoming less willing to retain their exposure to Bitcoin through asset managers, especially as Bitcoin’s price continues to slump further.

Although BlackRock has just suffered the largest withdrawal since it debuted its Bitcoin investment product, the record outflow did not alter its dominance in the market.

Further data shows that the BlackRock spot Bitcoin ETF still boasts a massive $47.82 billion in assets under management, spotlighting its leadership in the Bitcoin ETF market.

This positions it far ahead of Fidelity, which ranks as the second-largest Bitcoin ETF with just $10.62 billion in net assets.

  • Revenues for the quarter were a record $106.6 million, a 15% increase compared with $92.3 million in the third quarter of last year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Record revenue of $106.6 million, up 15%, with subscription revenue up 19% year-over-year;Four years of ongoing operating margin expansion to 23.8% in the quarter;.

AZOUR, Israel, Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ituran Location and Control Ltd. (NASDAQ: ITRN) today announced its consolidated financial results for the third quarter, ended September 30, 2026.

Highlights of the Third Quarter of 2026.

Revenues for the quarter were a record $106.6 million, a 15% increase compared with $92.3 million in the third quarter of last year.

76% of revenues were from location-based service subscription fees, and 24% were from product revenues.

Revenues from subscription fees for the quarter were $80.5 million, an increase of 19% over the third quarter of last year.

Product revenues for the quarter were $26.0 million, a 5% increase year-over-year.

Gross profit for the quarter was $55.4 million (52.0% of revenues), a 19% increase compared with $46.4 million (50.3% of revenues) in the third quarter of last year.

It has been revealed that gross margin on subscription revenues was 59.9%, compared to 60.1% in Q3 last year. The gross margin on product revenues improved to 27.7%, compared to 23.6% last year. The variance in the product gross margin between quarters reflects changes in the mix of products sold.

Operating income for the quarter was $25.4 million (23.8% of revenues), representing a 29% increase compared to $19.6 million (21.3% of revenues) in Q3 last year.

EBITDA for the quarter was $29.9 million (28.0% of revenues), up 21% from $24.6 million (26.7% of revenues) in the third quarter of last year.

Finance expenses for the quarter were $0.5 million, compared with finance expenses of $0.3 million in the third quarter of last year.

Net income for the third quarter of 2026 was $18.0 million (16.9% of revenues), or diluted earnings per share of $0.91, an increase of 23% compared to $14.6 million (15.9% of revenues), or $0.74 per diluted share, in the third quarter of last year.

Cash flow from operations for the quarter was $25.3 million.

On the balance sheet, as of September 30, 2026, the Manufacturer had net cash, including marketable securities, of $107.6 million, which includes no debt. This is compared with net cash, including marketable securities, of $103.7 million as of June 30, 2026 and $107.6 million as of year-end last year.

According to recent reports, the Board of Directors declared a dividend of $10 million for the quarter, or $0.50 per share. The current dividend takes into account the Company's continuing strong profitability, ongoing positive cash flow, and strong balance sheet.

During the third quarter, $1.9 million in shares were purchased under the Company's existing buy-back program. The total remaining authorization is $8.1 million. Share repurchases are funded by available cash and are made in accordance with SEC Rule 10b-18.

The Company will also be hosting a video conference call via the Zoom platform later today, Tuesday, November 24, 2026 at 9am Eastern Time and 4pm Israel Time.

On the call, management will review and discuss the results and will be available to answer investor questions.

To participate in the Zoom call, please register at the following link.https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_9R8KjpHlR4GccJZZdrYPEQ.

For those unable to listen to the live call, a replay of the call will be available from the day after the call in the investor relations section of Ituran's website.

According to recent reports, three XRP Ledger amendments linked to native lending have each gained two validator votes since Nov. 17, according to XRPScan data. As of Nov. 20, 2026, Single Asset Vault (XLS-65) had 25 votes, and Lending Protocol (XLS-66) and the LendingProtocolV1_1 patch had 24 votes each.

Industry observers note that XRPScan data shows that LendingProtocolV1_1 has been up for a vote since Sept. 29, 2026, when it came with the v3.4.0 release. According to the patch's voting history, it had about 19 votes for most of October. It started to gain votes again in late October. XRP was trading at $0.96 on Friday.

Lending is built directly into the XRP Ledger's code, with no third-party smart contracts. According to Ripple, lenders deposit into a Single Asset Vault, and the Lending Protocol lets loan brokers use that capital "to problem loans and track repayments onchain.".

In a recent development, the model is close to how banks lend. Loans have fixed terms and a repayment schedule, and credit brokers vet borrowers before the loans are issued. On Nov. 19, Clearpool revealed the full lending flow on the XRPL Devnet with Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin. In the demo, "An approved lender funds a private vault, and a borrower accepts and repays a loan underwritten offchain by a broker," Clearpool wrote.

Through Single Asset Vault (XLS-65), XRP holders will be able to deposit their coins into shared liquidity pools, and institutional borrowers will take loans from those pools at a fixed rate. After the loan is repaid, "the lender redeems at a higher share price," according to the Clearpool demo.

The amendments still need more votes before they can activate. "An amendment needs more than 80% support, held for 14 days, to activate," XRPScan indicates on its amendment pages. For the current set of 35 validators, the site puts the threshold at "more than 80% of 35 votes, so 29 needed.".

Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo open-source infrastructure shield to prevent AI-driven cyberattacks

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1170 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cybercriminals have gained the ability to discover vulnerabilities in software and take advantage of them in seconds, and it’s all thanks to artificial intelligence.
  • Sources indicate that they’ve just announced a new, open-source and extremely ambitious initiative called the Secure Infrastructure Project, which aims to ensure that all AI computing infrastructure is secure by design and capable of defending against lightning-fast AI-driven attacks.
  • In a blog post, Cisco Security Chief Technology Officer and Vice President of Engineering Thomas Graf explained that the industry has always treated security as an afterthought, essentially something that’s bolted onto systems after the fact.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:20 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

Cybercriminals have gained the ability to discover vulnerabilities in software and take advantage of them in seconds, and it’s all thanks to artificial intelligence. Enterprises need a better way to defend themselves, so it’s fitting that one of the world’s top AI companies, OpenAI Group PBC, together with Cisco Systems Inc., is stepping up with a solution.

Sources indicate that they’ve just announced a new, open-source and extremely ambitious initiative called the Secure Infrastructure Project, which aims to ensure that all AI computing infrastructure is secure by design and capable of defending against lightning-fast AI-driven attacks. The first project within that initiative is Shirudo, which is designed to protect infrastructure systems automatically from critical exploits before they can be patched.

In a blog post, Cisco Security Chief Technology Officer and Vice President of Engineering Thomas Graf explained that the industry has always treated security as an afterthought, essentially something that’s bolted onto systems after the fact. It has gotten away with this because much of the world’s computing infrastructure was built for workflows that proceed at human speeds. But with the emergence of AI models that can discover and work out how to exploit vulnerabilities in a matter of seconds, this kind of reactive security is no longer enough.

In a recent development, according to Graf, even now, when a major vulnerability is discovered in widely used software, it can take weeks or even months to come up with a fix and ensure that every major system is patched against it. “That timeframe is no longer acceptable given that the mean time to exploitation has become negative, meaning that a growing number of vulnerabilities are now being exploited before they are publicly disclosed,” he said. “This will only accelerate with the further evolution of AI models and cybersecurity capabilities, becoming the norm in open-weight models.”.

To counter these kinds of automated attacks, Cisco and OpenAI believe that infrastructure has to be rebuilt from scratch with security in mind. They argue that it’s time to abandon static defenses and embrace systems that are hardened by default, immutable and rebuildable from a previous “good” state, so users can quickly revert back in the event of an attack. To do this, infrastructure systems must be based on Trusted Platform Modules and utilize reinforcement learning techniques to safely test their own defenses so they can adapt when faced with novel cyberattacks from previously unknown vectors.

Graf stated the key to doing this is to secure workloads at runtime, which is why the initial focus of Cisco’s and OpenAI’s initiative is Shirudo, an evolution of the open-source Tetragon runtime security project that aims to provide autonomous defense for AI agents.

It has been revealed that shirudo, named after the Japanese word for “shield,” is based on extended Berkeley Packet Filter or eBPF, which is a Linux kernel technology that acts like a kind of sandbox within the operating system. Similar to how JavaScript makes web browsers programmable without a restart, eBPF enables small, verified programs to run inside the Linux kernel to observe an application’s activity and modify its behavior without altering its source code or rebooting it.

Graf explained that Cisco and OpenAI chose to use eBPF because there are no other real alternatives. Human-focused security consoles and policy languages are simply too slow for AI agents, and will limit their productivity.

By exposing programmable kernel interfaces, eBPF enables AI agents to capture granular telemetry, evaluate mitigations in monitoring mode and deploy cryptographically-signed shields in milliseconds. So cyberattacks that exploit unknown vulnerabilities can be blocked in real time without causing disruption to their live workloads.

“There is nothing more key than giving security teams the tools they need to match the speed of the AI-driven threats they are facing,” stated Cisco President and Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel. “We need self-defending infrastructure that acts at the speed of code, learns in real time and shields itself until patches are safely rolled out.”.

Sources indicate that openAI’s role in this is to prove that eBPF is up to the job, and it has already deployed Shirudo as part of an agentic control plane that’s powered by its Codex coding agent. When given details of a newly introduced vulnerability, Codex can use Shirudo to autonomously build an exploit reproducer and then design a mitigation strategy. It then validates the mitigation code and deploys the cryptographically-signed shields across all affected nodes.

The two partners recently tested Shirudo against a critical new vulnerability in OpenJDK called Java4Shell, and it was able to rapidly generate Java bytecode that it injected directly into a running Elasticsearch agent to block malicious Base64 overwrites that would have compromised the system.

Sources indicate that openAI co-founder and President Greg Brockman said the goal of Shirudo is to help companies protect their systems from new threats until they can build and deploy a more durable patch. “When one team finds a better way to protect a system, others shouldn’t have to start from scratch,” he explained.

To that end, Cisco and OpenAI say they’re welcoming developers, kernel engineers, platform builders and security experts to collaborate on Shirudo and other initiatives within their broader Secure Infrastructure Project.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Global survey finds 40% of firms aim to offer near-23-hour trading by year-end, while 42% have yet to determine how they will cover extended sessions operationally.

According to recent reports, UPCOMING YORK, Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As U.S. equities move toward a longer trading day, a gap is emerging between the ability to execute an overnight trade and the operations needed to support it. A global industry pulse survey by Broadridge (NYSE: BR), SIFMA and The ValueExchange finds that 40% of firms intend to offer near-23-hour, five-day-a-week trading by the end of 2026, while 42% have not yet determined how they will cover extended sessions operationally.

Industry observers note that "An overnight trade does not end when it is executed, firms also need the people, controls and technology to monitor exceptions and support the trade through settlement," stated Quentin Limouzi, Global Head of Post Trade at Broadridge. "Broadridge's systems are operational during extended trading hours. Now is the time for firms to make sure their people, processes and technology are ready to support those trades from execution through settlement. As demand grows, the market won't wait for the back office to catch up.".

"Extended trading hours could give investors more opportunities to respond to events and access U.S. markets," stated Steve Byron, Managing Director and Head of Technology, Operations and BCP at SIFMA. "But a resilient market depends on more than an open trading window. The industry must work together to understand the implications for liquidity, operations and the infrastructure that supports investors around the clock.".

The October 2026 survey of 268 financial institutions points to a central tension: the ability to execute an overnight trade does not necessarily mean the services, controls and operational coverage around it are ready to operate continuously.

Demand is not simply a question of adding more time to the trading day. Respondents identified the ability to trade overnight and to react to geopolitical events as leading objectives. At the same time, only 10% expected liquidity to be adequate for institutional-size execution from day one, suggesting a selective early market rather than an immediate shift of all trading activity.

Firms should assess their readiness across people, processes and technology now, and engage providers to address the operational gaps that extended trading hours may expose.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:43 amNovember 17, 2026 at 11:43 am.
  • Seattle police already have a dog that sniffs out tech.
  • Recent findings suggest that the department’s Arson/Bomb Squad is now using a Spot robot from Boston Dynamics, bought with a Federal Emergency Management Agency grant that the Seattle City Council approved in April after a review of privacy and security risks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:43 amNovember 17, 2026 at 11:43 am.

Seattle police already have a dog that sniffs out tech. Now they’ve got a piece of tech that looks like a dog.

Recent findings suggest that the department’s Arson/Bomb Squad is now using a Spot robot from Boston Dynamics, bought with a Federal Emergency Management Agency grant that the Seattle City Council approved in April after a review of privacy and security risks. Bomb technicians can steer the robot from nearly a mile away to inspect suspicious devices, open doors and move possible explosives into safe containers, SPD noted in a blog post last week.

It’s a big upgrade for the squad, which has handled more than 600 calls so far this year. SPD’s main bomb robot is nearly 20 years old, weighs more than 100 pounds and rolls on tracks, and it can only be hauled around in the squad’s mobile workshop. Spot weighs under 100 pounds, climbs stairs and rides in a pickup truck that bomb techs drive daily.

SPD also spelled out what Spot won’t do.

The robot will only be used for explosive threats in the city and at the port, and it won’t carry a weapon. SPD said a weapon would go against Boston Dynamics’ rules for its robots. Spot’s 360-degree camera sends an encrypted live feed to the operator but doesn’t record or use facial recognition.

In a recent development, the only thing the robot does on its own is open a door, after an operator lines it up. As one bomb technician put it in SPD’s post, Spot will “be as dumb in 10 years as it is today.”.

It’s not the first time SPD has turned to a four-legged partner for tech-related work.

Nala, an electronic storage detection K9 — profiled by GeekWire in 2024 — is trained to smell a chemical compound used in making electronics. The Labrador retriever helps SPD’s Internet Crimes Against Children task force find hidden phones, hard drives and micro SD cards during warrant searches. Her handler, Det. Daljit Gill, told GeekWire at the time that Nala turns up a device human searchers missed about 30% of the time.

Spot appears decidedly less cuddly.

According to recent reports, boston Dynamics, maker of backflipping Atlas humanoids and other viral-video robots, first unveiled the robodog in 2015. A smaller, all-electric version followed a year later.

The machines have long stirred dystopian unease. A 2017 “Black Mirror” episode featured killer robot dogs inspired by the firm’s designs. Still, Spot has turned up in friendlier settings: then-Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos walked one at the company’s MARS conference in 2018 — a scene described by GeekWire’s Alan Boyle as featuring the “anxiety-inducing” robot.

In a recent development, police departments have embraced the robots, too. More than 60 bomb squads and SWAT teams in the U.S. and Canada use Spot, Bloomberg reported last year, including a regional bomb unit in Portland. New York police returned one in 2021 after public backlash, then brought the robots back two years later.

Back in Seattle, SPD’s bomb technicians see more potential uses down the road, according to the department’s post, including communicating and observing from a distance as part of de-escalation. For now, Spot’s job is limited to explosives.

And the robot won’t be getting a new name, SPD stated, “because it is not a toy, or a dog, even though it kind of looks like both.”.

NEW YORK, Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- IPVanish has been recognized by Expert Consumers for its privacy protection capabilities, independent no-logs verification, and security features as online shopping activity increases during the 2026 Black Friday season.

IPVanish is also offering promotional subscription pricing across its Essential, Complete, and Advanced plans, providing different options based on consumer security requirements and budgets.

IPVanish Recognized for Privacy Protection and Independent Verification.

Privacy transparency remains an crucial consideration when selecting a virtual private network. A VPN encrypts internet traffic between a connected device and a VPN server, helping protect information from exposure across local networks. The technology also masks the original IP address, providing another layer of privacy during everyday browsing.

IPVanish has strengthened its privacy commitments through recurring independent assessments of its no-logs policy. In November 2026, the organization declared the results of its third independent no-logs audit, following earlier assessments conducted in 2022 and 2025. The latest assessment was completed on September 25, 2026. (Schellman Compliance, September 2026)).

The audit found no evidence of traffic, metadata, or session logging that contradicted the manufacturer's stated no-logs policy. These findings provide additional support for IPVanish's position that customer internet activity is not recorded through its VPN infrastructure.

It has been revealed that independent verification is particularly relevant because privacy policies represent commitments that require meaningful evaluation. An external assessment provides an opportunity to examine whether actual operational practices align with published privacy statements. Although an audit cannot guarantee complete anonymity or eliminate every online security risk, recurring assessments contribute to greater transparency.

It has been revealed that IPVanish also continues to develop its server infrastructure, including a transition toward RAM-only servers. This infrastructure approach is designed to prevent persistent information storage on server hardware because data held in volatile memory is erased when a server restarts. The transition is expected to continue through 2027.

Security Features Support Safer Online Shopping.

Industry observers note that online shopping frequently involves accessing accounts, entering personal details, and completing transactions across different internet connections. A VPN can help protect connection-level information, particularly when browsing through public Wi-Fi networks in locations such as airports, hotels, cafes, and shopping centers.

It has been revealed that IPVanish supports modern VPN protocols, including WireGuard and OpenVPN. These protocols provide secure connection options while supporting everyday browsing and other internet activities. Encryption helps prevent unauthorized parties on local networks from easily reading transmitted information.

The service also includes a kill switch designed to block internet traffic if the VPN connection unexpectedly drops. This feature helps prevent an unprotected connection from continuing without the user's knowledge. DNS leak protection provides another safeguard by helping keep DNS requests within the protected VPN connection.

These capabilities can be useful during major shopping events, when consumers frequently visit retailer websites, compare product prices, and access payment accounts. However, VPN protection addresses only certain online risks. It does not independently prevent phishing attempts, fraudulent websites, malicious software, or retailer data breaches.

Industry observers note that IPVanish also supports unlimited simultaneous device connections. The feature allows a single subscription to cover multiple supported devices without requiring separate accounts for each connection. This arrangement can accommodate households using smartphones, tablets, laptops, and desktop computers for different online activities.

Recent findings suggest that device flexibility is particularly relevant as shopping increasingly takes place across mobile and desktop platforms. Consumers can maintain VPN protection while moving between devices, provided the appropriate applications are installed and configured.

Online Privacy Remains an Important Consumer Consideration.

The expansion of digital commerce has made internet privacy an increasingly relevant part of everyday technology use. IPVanish's recognition by Expert Consumers reflects the importance of independently evaluated privacy practices, connection security, and accessible subscription options. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former National Association of Realtors Chief Financial Officer John Pierpoint has sued the organization for unpaid retirement compensation totaling more than $541,000, according to a complaint filed on Tuesday.
  • In a recent development, pierpoint alleged NAR has paid senior vice presidents one year of their base salary at retirement since 2005.
  • Pierpoint retired from NAR on March 31, 2025 — a date he chose with the 2023 Sitzer | Burnett buyer-broker commission lawsuit in mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former National Association of Realtors Chief Financial Officer John Pierpoint has sued the organization for unpaid retirement compensation totaling more than $541,000, according to a complaint filed on Tuesday.

In a recent development, pierpoint alleged NAR has paid senior vice presidents one year of their base salary at retirement since 2005. To avoid booking the full expense when a senior vice president retired, NAR created a Compensation Reserve that let it steadily set aside funds throughout the executive’s tenure, which it would release at retirement. Pierpoint helped establish the reserve in 2005 at the direction of former NAR CEO Dale Stinton, court documents said.

Pierpoint retired from NAR on March 31, 2025 — a date he chose with the 2023 Sitzer | Burnett buyer-broker commission lawsuit in mind. The former CFO said he was key in executing the buyer-broker commission settlement payout, which totaled $418 million. The first settlement payment, totaling roughly $200 million, was issued in February 2025, with subsequent payments of $72 million per year until the full $418 million is paid.

Pierpoint said he notified NAR of his impending retirement in late 2024 and requested his retirement payout. However, six days before his last day with NAR, Pierpoint alleged that a Grant Thornton auditor named White — there is no first name listed in the court documents — emailed him and said that “NAR had been ‘unable to locate any policy or verify any consistent practice’ concerning the Compensation Reserve or ‘the payout to executives of a full year of salary upon retirement.'”.

Sources indicate that white also allegedly said that the Compensation Reserve “was not used to fund” the exit packages of eight other senior vice presidents who retired before Pierpoint, which are listed in the court documents as L.J., F.S., B.M., D.H., J.G.,  J.B., D.G. and B.G. Real Estate News said L.J., D.G. and B.G. are likely former general counsel Laurie Janik, former SVP of talent development and resources Donna Gland, and former senior vice president and CEO Bob Goldberg.

As a result, Grant Thornton mentioned it was “unable to approve the payout of a full year’s compensation without any concrete proof that such act is mandated by an employment agreement, policy or plan.”.

Pierpoint claimed NAR had the funds to pay his retirement benefit and provided a ledger outlining what the Association allegedly reserved from December 2014 to December 2024. He also stated the trial balances NAR provided to outside auditors, including Grant Thornton, included evidence of the Compensation Reserve’s existence and purpose.

It has been revealed that “NAR carried its obligation to Pierpoint at approximately 97.6 cents on the dollar three months before it refused to pay him anything,” the complaint read. “The practice NAR now claims it cannot verify is documented in NAR’s own ledger, its own year-end schedules, its own payroll records and its own audit files, and was paid to every one of Pierpoint’s predecessors who retired. NAR did not stop believing in its obligation; it stopped wanting to pay it.”.

Visualized with the help of AI.

Recent findings suggest that pierpoint’s counsel accused NAR of shirking its obligation to pay the former CFO due to its financial woes after the settlement. In December 2025, former NAR president Kevin Sears remarked the buyer-broker commission settlement saved the Association’s finances — the other option was to file an appeal and declare bankruptcy.

“John Pierpoint helped guide NAR through an extraordinarily challenging period in its history, including the financial consequences of the antitrust litigation,” remarked David Fish, an attorney with Workplace Law Partners, P.C., who represents Pierpoint. “After nearly four decades of service, he expected the organization to honor the same retirement compensation practice it had followed for other senior executives.”.

“We believe the evidence will establish that the financial pressures following the antitrust verdict did not relieve NAR of its obligation to pay compensation earned by its employees,” he added.

It has been revealed that pierpoint’s counsel is requesting that NAR pay the $541,059 retirement payout, statutory damages of 5 percent of the unpaid amount for each month it remains unpaid, attorneys’ fees and costs, and prejudgment and post-judgment interest. They also seek a jury trial.

NAR denied Pierpoint’s claims, saying that the former CFO has “[mischaracterized] a varied set of individual arrangements with departing executives as a uniform and guaranteed retirement benefit.”.

It has been revealed that “Mr. Pierpoint was not entitled to the payment he now seeks, and NAR’s decision was unrelated to its antitrust settlement or its financial condition,” an NAR spokesperson told Inman in an emailed statement. “NAR is committed to appropriate financial controls and responsible stewardship of its members’ dues dollars. NAR pays compensation and benefits that are actually owed, not just because a former executive requests payment. No such obligation exists here, and we intend to vigorously defend against these claims through the appropriate legal process.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the company's commercial phased array delivered a mission-grade telemetry, tracking, and control (TT&C) link to a U.S. Government satellite in GEO, via the Joint Antenna Marketplace.

TORRANCE, Calif., Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Northwood Space Corp. ("Northwood") today unveiled completion of the key technical milestone of a prototype contract with the U.S. Space Force's (USSF) Space Systems Command (SSC), through the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Battle Management Command, Control, Communications and Space Intelligence (BMC3I).

The key milestone involved a series of full-duplex TT&C contacts with a U.S. Government satellite in geosynchronous orbit (GEO), using Northwood's Portal phased array antenna. Northwood's network met the program's technical objectives within a year of award, with receive and transmit performance sufficient to command and control the spacecraft. Previous milestones included live-sky, full-duplex communications with a satellite in low Earth orbit (LEO).

Under the award with BMC3I, Northwood delivered advanced, assured connectivity services on its network, supporting the Space Force's augmentation from the Satellite Control Network (SCN) toward next-generation ground architecture. The operations for the key milestone ran through BMC3I's Joint Antenna Marketplace (JAM), a cloud-based system that improves satellite scheduling, resiliency and scalability through competitive prototyping. The combined commercial and government team onboarded the newly introduced site and the mission partner's configuration into the system in a matter of hours.

"GEO satellites carry some of the most critical government and commercial missions, and they're some of the hardest links to close," stated Bridgit Mendler, co-founder and CEO of Northwood. "Our Portal system has now closed those links, building on earlier demonstrated capability in LEO. We engineered it for these hard, high-stakes missions, where government and commercial operators need assured TT&C across orbits, and we're proud to support Space Force PAE BMC3I and SSC's System Delta 85 in delivering this capability.".

Northwood's global ground station network, consisting of multi-beam phased array and high-throughput parabolic antennas, is purpose-built for diverse missions in contested operating environments, enabling simultaneous connections across LEO, medium Earth orbit (MEO), and GEO while delivering scalable capacity through commercial service agreements. This lets government and commercial operators add ground capacity rapidly, as missions need it. With the prototype complete, Northwood is eligible for a transition from prototype to production.

Northwood is building the network connecting spacecraft to Earth, starting with satellite ground stations. The software-defined, shared network lets customers connect with their entire fleet in hours instead of the years it would take to build their own ground network. Trusted by organizations and programs across commercial and U.S. and allied government space operators, Northwood delivers reliable, resilient, high-throughput links so operators are free to execute any mission and go further and faster.

Microsoft jabs at OpenAI and Anthropic, touting cheaper, customizable AI models of its own

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:57 amNovember 17, 2026 at 12:33 pm.
  • Industry observers note that microsoft is a partner and investor in both OpenAI and Anthropic, and it sells their AI models to its own customers.
  • “Simply stated, anything you can do in Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot and for less,” noted Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft’s commercial business, during the opening keynote at the organization’s annual conference for IT professionals and business customers in San Francisco.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:57 amNovember 17, 2026 at 12:33 pm.

Industry observers note that microsoft is a partner and investor in both OpenAI and Anthropic, and it sells their AI models to its own customers. But another role was on full display during the company’s Ignite keynote Tuesday: competitor.

“Simply stated, anything you can do in Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot and for less,” noted Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft’s commercial business, during the opening keynote at the organization’s annual conference for IT professionals and business customers in San Francisco.

In a recent development, jacob Andreou, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, went further. “We’ve all seen Anthropic and OpenAI embrace documents, slides, and spreadsheets, but their simplified viewers and editors force compromise on power and collaboration,” he mentioned.

The full versions of Word, Excel and PowerPoint inside Copilot are included in the subscription. “That means that Copilot is the only way to draft a PowerPoint presentation without spinning a meter,” Andreou said.

According to recent reports, microsoft’s cost comparison: Andreou backed up the pitch with a chart of estimated monthly costs per business user, including subscription and usage fees. It put Copilot at $30 for an “everyday” AI user, compared with $81 for ChatGPT and $205 for Claude.

It has been revealed that for “advanced” users of each organization’s agent tools, it indicated $96 for Copilot, $149 for ChatGPT and $299 for Claude. Most of the Claude figure is estimated usage charges on top of Anthropic’s $20 enterprise seat.

Recent findings suggest that the numbers come from research Microsoft commissioned and paid for from GigaOm, based on testing Microsoft ran in October on modeled workloads. They reflect enterprise pricing, which adds usage charges to a per-seat fee, not the flat monthly subscriptions that individuals pay for ChatGPT and Claude.

Partners and rivals: The pitch comes as Anthropic expands into Microsoft’s core business. Last week it introduced upcoming Claude-based tools for spreadsheets and whiteboards that compete more directly with Office. The organization is expected to make its IPO this week, putting new scrutiny on its financials and long-term growth prospects.

Recent findings suggest that the companies’ products are also intertwined. Anthropic’s Claude for Microsoft 365, for example, lets people use Claude inside Office apps for tasks such as sorting email and creating slide decks.

The product has less than a tenth as many weekly customers as the paid version of Copilot in Office, The Information reported Monday, citing internal Microsoft data. Andreou is one of the executives who see that as a sign Microsoft can keep customers from switching, the report said.

New MAI models: Microsoft AI also released a new batch of its own MAI models, built to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic for a fraction of the price. It’s a notable stance, given that Microsoft still sells their models, too. On the same stage, CEO Satya Nadella announced that OpenAI’s GPT-6.2, released Tuesday morning, is now available in Microsoft Foundry.

In a recent development, the lineup includes MAI Code 2, available in GitHub Copilot starting Tuesday. Microsoft notes it delivers 96% of the coding performance of Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the price, on benchmarks Microsoft chose.

It has been revealed that microsoft also introduced MAI Cyber 2 Flash, a security model it says matches OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra on one benchmark at less than 2% of the cost per task. Other newly introduced models cover image editing, live speech and transcription.

Industry observers note that the other new business: MAI Licensed Weights. Companies can take a Microsoft AI model, customize it with their own data and run it in their own Azure environment, with help from Microsoft’s Frontier Company consulting arm. AT&T used an earlier version of the program, Custom Models, to build a MAI model for 5G network analytics.

It’s the latest step in Microsoft’s push for what Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has called “long term self-sufficiency,” which started with seven homegrown models at Build in June.

In a recent development, keeping costs in check: The cost theme ran through the keynote. In a demo, Althoff revealed Copilot building a keynote outline, a slide deck and a customer tracker for a retail conference, plus an agent he named Amelia to keep the work going.

Industry observers note that the cost of his two-hour Sunday session: about 10,000 credits, or roughly $100. Althoff presented that as a bargain compared with the staff time it would have taken: “my team hits the ground running for NRF without me bothering them,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft is also selling tools to keep that bill in check. A fresh Agent 365 Business Analytics feature demonstrates business leaders what’s driving their AI spending and what they’re getting for it, and a companion Cost Management tool lets IT set spending policies and get alerts. Microsoft cited a McKinsey survey in which 93% of respondents reported exceeding their AI budgets.

In a recent development, in another notable announcement, Microsoft and Salesforce unveiled “Copilotforce,” bringing Salesforce customer data and actions into Copilot, Teams and Fabric. The Copilot plugin is available in preview.

Earlier, Nadella opened the keynote by addressing last week’s global Outlook outage.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:29 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

It has been revealed that crowdStrike Holdings Inc. today announced plans to acquire Zscaler Inc., a fellow provider of cybersecurity software, for about $43.9 billion.

Sources indicate that the all-stock deal values the latter organization at $260.40 per share. That’s a 34% premium to Zscaler’s closing price on Friday, the day CrowdStrike’s takeover interest became public. The transaction would be the largest cybersecurity acquisition on record by a wide margin.

According to recent reports, investors weren’t entirely thrilled. CrowdStrike’s shares fell 9% today, an indication that might think it’s an awfully large pill to swallow. Zscaler’s stock, however, rose almost 18%.

The companies reported their quarterly results in conjunction with the acquisition announcement. Both topped expectations across the board. CrowdStrike posted adjusted net income of $354.9 million on $1.58 billion in revenue, while Zscaler reported a $208.4 million adjusted profit and sales of $949.3 million. The former company also boosted its full-year guidance.

CrowdStrike’s flagship Falcon platform uses lightweight programs called sensors to protect employee devices, cloud instances and other technology assets. Zscaler’s Zero Trust Exchange, in turn, protects the network connections that link together those assets. The platform is positioned as an alternative to virtual private network tools.

It has been revealed that the product portfolios of CrowdStrike’s and Zscaler overlap in some areas. Both companies offer tools that can protect artificial intelligence applications from threats such as prompt injections. They also compete in the secure browser category, although their respective offerings take different approaches to blocking malware.

Zscaler offers a tool that can automatically launch simulated cyberattacks against applications to find weak points. CrowdStrike joined the fray as well earlier this year with SafeMind, a set of custom AI models and related assets. It not only finds software vulnerabilities but also develops detections, automated workflows designed to spot hacking attempts.

Recent findings suggest that crowdStrike said that it will use the network telemetry collected by Zscaler to enhance SafeMind’s training dataset. In 2024, the latter firm disclosed that its platform blocked more than 9 billion threats per day. That activity, which has no doubt grown in volume since, should give CrowdStrike’s AI models a more complete understanding of hacker behavior.

Sources indicate that the tech giant’s looks for Zscaler also extend beyond AI training. CrowdStrike will incorporate the network protection provider’s software into its Flex offering, which enables customers to buy multiple cybersecurity tools via a single contract. That could help expand the adoption of Zscaler’s products among CrowdStrike customers.

It has been revealed that the companies have also identified other upselling opportunities. They disclosed today that about 8,000 Zscaler customers don’t yet use CrowdStrike products.

“With Zscaler, we’re building cybersecurity’s operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely,” remarked CrowdStrike founder and Chief Executive Officer George Kurtz (pictured). “We see a path to become the largest AI safety and security firm the world has ever seen.”.

In a recent development, crowdStrike expects to complete the acquisition in the second half of its 2028 fiscal year, which starts next February. The company stated that the deal will be “significantly and immediately accretive” to free cash flow per share upon closing.

CrowdStrike expects Zscaler’s financial impact to grow over time. It estimates that the deal will unlock $500 million worth of annual cost synergies within 18 to 24 months, mainly in the form of data center, supplier and operational improvements. The firm also sees Zscaler boosting its annual revenue run-rate by $1 billion within 30 months.

Human review remains paramount for AI mortgage underwriting

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that artificial intelligence is helping mortgage lenders and due-diligence firms review loan files and extract borrower information, but integrating AI into underwriting processes isn’t a one-and-done experience.
  • Industry observers note that at Incenter Diligence Solutions, AI has accelerated document indexing and data extraction, according to president Pamela Hamrick.
  • According to recent reports, hamrick noted that while AI can extract information from standardized mortgage documents like loan estimates and closing disclosures, borrower-provided records — including pay stubs and bank statements.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that artificial intelligence is helping mortgage lenders and due-diligence firms review loan files and extract borrower information, but integrating AI into underwriting processes isn’t a one-and-done experience. The technology still needs human oversight, experts say, especially when loans involve unusual circumstances or require judgment beyond standard guidelines.

Industry observers note that at Incenter Diligence Solutions, AI has accelerated document indexing and data extraction, according to president Pamela Hamrick. Technology can now sort and categorize thousands of pages of loan documents in minutes, replacing a process that once required employees to manually separate and label files.

According to recent reports, hamrick noted that while AI can extract information from standardized mortgage documents like loan estimates and closing disclosures, borrower-provided records — including pay stubs and bank statements. — are harder to process because their formats vary.

AI, however, can identify inconsistencies across documents and summarize them for underwriters to investigate.

“The technology is identifying the questions, and the inconsistencies and the anomalies, between all of this documentation, and summarizing that for an underwriter or a reviewer … to dig deeper and make a decision about whether or not what the AI has identified is a real risk — or if it’s a minimal risk or maybe it’s no risk at all because of the particular scenario,” Hamrick remarked in an interview with HousingWire.

Julia Curran, senior managing director of residential AI products at SitusAMC, said the organization uses AI to re-underwrite closed loans in the secondary market, checking regulatory and underwriting guidelines as well as data accuracy before loans are reviewed for securitization.

In a recent development, according to Curran, SitusAMC builds AI agents around processes established by human subject matter experts and tests their results against loans previously reviewed by people. She said the company runs repeated tests until the system reaches at least 95% accuracy.

According to recent reports, but the technology still needs the human touch. Curran said the system sends blank or inconsistent fields to human reviewers, and final credit decisions require judgments that cannot be reduced to individual data points.

“A final credit decision shouldn’t be made by the machine because there’s other things to consider besides the specific data points,” Curran mentioned.

Hamrick added: “Companies that fully rely on AI are potentially going to have misses in some other areas where a human might have been able to make a different decision.”.

Recent findings suggest that curran also warned about the AI model supplying information not supported or provided by the documents submitted. She described a case in which a model supplied a solar panel number that was not included in a particular loan file. The answer was correct, but the system had apparently drawn on information from other files.

“Even though it’s right, I don’t want that answer,” Curran said. “I want to stay within the four walls of this file.”.

The executives mentioned lenders should test AI against established human processes before relying on it for underwriting.

Hamrick recommended introducing the technology in one part of the workflow at a time, comparing its results with human reviews before expanding its use. She also said lenders should prepare employees for changes by retraining them for tasks that require more human intervention.

“The best thing that we can do as leaders is look where the technology can ultimately take over, and then take the folks that are doing those roles and train them to be better at the things that require more human intervention,” she said.

Curran said quality control requires testing models across different loan types and scenarios. SitusAMC maintains a test bank of hundreds of previously reviewed loans, including purchases, refinances, adjustable-rate mortgages and loans with rate buydowns. When a model changes, the organization runs its prompts against the test bank to check whether results remain consistent.

In a recent development, these tests add costs that lenders may overlook. Curran said companies should ask AI vendors how their systems were developed, whether subject matter experts helped establish the processes and whether ongoing regression testing is in place.

“You want the same answer every time,” Curran stated. “The process of taking a non-deterministic process and making it deterministic takes a lot of time and effort.”.

HELSINKI, Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CGI (TSX: GIB.A) (NYSE: GIB), one of the largest independent IT and business consulting services firms in the world, has confirmed that an artificial intelligence (AI) solution, CGI AI Head Analysis, developed in partnership with Helsinki University Hospital (HUS) and Planmeca, has received official certification as a medical device under the European Union Medical Device Regulation (MDR class IIb). The AI solution supports physicians in detecting brain hemorrhages from computed tomography (CT) scans.

CGI AI Head Analysis analyzes head CT images to detect non-traumatic, spontaneous intracranial  hemorrhages and flags suspected acute blood on the images. It is easy for physicians to quickly review suspicious findings marked by artificial intelligence. The solution is particularly well suited for situations where a doctor performing diagnostics on head CT images wants to rule out that no potentially life-threatening intracranial hemorrhages go unnoticed, for example, in busy emergency rooms.

According to recent reports, the MDR certification is a major milestone that enables hospitals to deploy the solution at scale. The certification confirms that the solution meets strict national and EU-level standards for safety, quality, and performance. The approval is also an important recognition to the long-term collaboration in which globally scalable and high-quality technology solutions are developed based on scientific evidence. During the development, scientific articles related to the solution have been published in internationally respected scientific journals.

According to recent reports, "This is a historic achievement that we've worked toward for years at HUS and with CGI and Planmeca. The scientific basis of algorithms is exceptionally strong, making the solution highly reliable in quality. This phase of the project is a demonstration that we can make dozens, if not hundreds, of accurate diagnostic imaging algorithms in the future â in a short time. I think this is just the beginning," says Dr. Miikka Korja, Chief Physician and Associate Professor of Neurosurgery, at HUS, who led the project.

"Achieving MDR approval demonstrates that this AI solution is not just innovative but ready for real-world clinical use. It can now be integrated directly into hospital imaging workflows and decision-making," indicates Sonja PietilÃ¤, Vice-President Consulting Expert, leading the solution development at CGI.

HUS is one of the largest hospitals in Europe and the second largest employer in Finland. The Department of Neurosurgery is one of the most well-known and visited neurosurgery departments in the world.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 17, 2026 at 1:36 pmNovember 20, 2026 at 5:15 pm.

Seattle startup Aarden AI on Tuesday unveiled $8 million in newly introduced funding to grow its team and accelerate its work helping landowners evaluate potential uses for their properties and navigate deals with developers building data centers, clean energy projects, housing and other projects.

Founded last year, the company says its clients collectively own or manage approximately 14 million acres worldwide — nearly the land area of West Virginia. Aarden’s team said it has evaluated more than $500 million worth of land deals.

Recent findings suggest that “But land markets remain opaque and manual with far too much friction. Finding the right site, and building trust with the right partners promptly, is more important than ever for our economy and our environment,” founder and CEO Danan Margason said in a statement.

The company combines data on hundreds of land attributes with historical market data and proprietary models to assess development suitability, valuation trends, ownership and community sentiment. Its tools and services also help developers identify sites and connect with landowners.

Aarden generates revenue through subscriptions to its technology, which includes AI-native data, models and investment tools, and through fees for services tied to specific deals or analyses.

The latest funding brings Aarden’s total investments to $12 million. Overture Ventures led the round, with participation from Madrona and Propeller Ventures. The startup previously raised $4 million in a round led by Planeteer in June 2025. The company has 13 employees and plans to nearly double in size over the next 12 months.

Margason said he debuted the business on the premise that while there have long been tools to support developers, landowners have been largely on their own to evaluate and optimize deals so they’re not taken advantage of or end up partnering with untrustworthy organizations.

One customer, timberland investment manager Resource Management Service, uses Aarden to evaluate whether tracts are best suited for continued timber production, conservation, solar development or other uses.

“Diligence that used to take months now produces investment-grade answers we can act on, and that is shaping how we manage value across our portfolio,” said Alex Hinson, president and CEO of Resource Management Service.

Other companies offering property research and analysis tools include Acres, which provides land data, valuations and due diligence tools, and Land id, which offers property insights and mapping tools.

Ben Eidelson, a partner at Stepchange Ventures, which participated in the startup’s first funding round, stated the firm is already having an impact.

“We now have the capability to make smarter decisions about land, optimizing for the outcomes that matter from conservation to the local economy,” Eidelson stated on LinkedIn.
