Liquidations on crypto exchanges reached $1.57 billion over 24 hours on Nov. 20, according to CoinGlass data. Bitcoin (BTC) fell 4.11% to $59,370, its lowest level since July 2.

According to CoinGlass, 265,525 traders were liquidated over 24 hours, and long positions accounted for $1.43 billion of the total.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin saw $554.28 million in liquidations, and 91.3% of that amount came from long positions. Ethereum (ETH) fell below $1,700 on Nov. 20, and ETH traders saw $331.08 million in liquidations. Binance accounted for 45.8% of all liquidations, and the largest single order was also on Binance: an $11.98 million ETHUSDT long position that was liquidated at $1,638.78.

XRP saw $14.67 million in liquidations, and $13.86 million of that amount came from long positions.

Recent findings suggest that stock markets fell on the same day. The Nasdaq Composite has given back all of its gains for 2026, and the S&P 500 fell 1.82% to 7,045.5 points. The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones are now down 10% from their record highs. The VIX volatility index jumped 8.09% to 30.73.

Nvidia has lost $2.55 trillion in market value since its Oct. 6 peak. Anthropic shares started trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 19. On Nov. 20, the stock fell about 10% in premarket trading, and it was close to its IPO price of $83.

In a recent development, nvidia futures on crypto exchanges saw $26.79 million in liquidations, according to CoinGlass. Anthropic contracts saw $15.29 million in liquidations, and 90.7% of that amount came from long positions.

On Nov. 19, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said on CNBC that investors had been moving money from crypto into big listings. "People are taking liquidity out of a very liquid market, crypto included — Bitcoin, XRP — and moving it into SpaceX. The exact same thing happened coming into the Anthropic IPO," he said. Garlinghouse also expected a crypto rally after the listing. "I think you'll see that happen here as well," he said.

According to recent reports, gold fell 2.27% to $3,542.12 an ounce, and silver dropped 3.51% to $41.32. The gold-to-silver ratio rose 1.43% to 85.686.

Gold and silver futures on crypto platforms saw $64.9 million and $40.3 million in liquidations, respectively.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AKT stakers are close to approving Akash's move from Cosmos to Solana, with Mintscan projecting a pass at 97.2% yes as voting enters its final hours.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

AKT stakers are close to approving Akash's move from Cosmos to Solana, with Mintscan projecting a pass at 97.2% yes as voting enters its final hours.

But a yes on Proposal 346 opens a door rather than completing a move. Before a single AKT reaches Solana, two independent audits and at least two more on-chain votes still have to happen.

Sources indicate that the summary going around is simple: Akash is leaving Cosmos for Solana. The proposal itself is narrower than that, and the details matter for anyone holding AKT.

Proposal 346 on akashnet-2, titled "Migrate the Akash Protocol to Solana," closes at 15:02 UTC on November 2. A yes vote approves the migration blueprint and authorises AKT to launch as an SPL token through a one-way portal that stays open for two years. It does not set a cutover date, it does not move a single lease, and on its own it does not open the portal.

The technical spec for that portal was published the day after voting opened. It reveals how many further steps lie between this vote and a working SPL AKT.

The proposal text in Akash's AEP repository says a yes vote does two things:.

It also says plainly what it doesn't do: "it does not set a cutover date and does not move the marketplace." Live leases, staking and governance on akashnet-2 continue as normal. The marketplace moves only after audits and rehearsals pass and "a separate cutover proposal passes on this chain.".

In a recent development, A no vote would stop the whole plan. In the proposal's words: "Nothing moves; the token does not launch and the program returns to option analysis.".

At 08:43 UTC on November 2, about six hours before voting closed, Mintscan's page for Proposal 346 showed an expected result of "Will PASS":.

Industry observers note that turnout stood at 68.80% of bonded stake, against a quorum of 33.40%. The same figures can be read from Akash's own chain API, through the proposal object and its tally endpoint.

Mintscan's 97.2% is yes as a share of all votes cast. Akash's pass threshold leaves abstentions out, and on that basis yes stands at about 98.7%, far above the 50% needed. The veto share is negligible.

Industry observers note that the tally has barely changed since early morning. A read of the chain at 07:29 UTC showed almost exactly the same totals, with only a handful of AKT added to the yes side. With turnout and margin that large, the outcome is not in doubt. The more useful question is what happens after it passes.

Industry observers note that the portal's design is in AEP-95, "One-Way AKT Sink to Solana,", a draft published on October 27 by core developers Artur Troian and Joseph Chalabi. It describes a "deliberately one-way" bridge with no return path. The authors say this removes "the largest class of bridge attacks.".

Why supply doesn't change: every SPL AKT is backed by AKT locked on Akash, and nothing is minted independently on Solana. The token is a legacy SPL mint with six decimals and no freeze authority.

The spec's own risk table names the biggest trust point. The upgrade authority over the Solana programs could "mint without limit." That power is meant to sit with a time-locked multisig appointed by Akash governance, with monitors set to alert on every admin action.

At launch, SPL AKT has no protocol role. It will support "transfers and DEX liquidity only, with no staking or governance rights." Inflation stays on Akash. To seed trading, Overclock Labs, Akash's core developer, will send 1 million AKT through the bridge to a Solana treasury vault. That deposit follows the same rules as everyone else's.

According to recent reports, proposal 346 requires "two independent audits of the token and portal code before launch," with reports published within 30 days. AEP-95's launch sequence highlights what that requirement means on-chain.

Sources indicate that so Proposal 346 is the first of at least five on-chain decisions. The "2 to 3 weeks" launch estimate depends on the audits finishing and the upgrade and parameter votes passing on schedule.

Sources indicate that for now, nothing. The proposal's disclosures set out what changes later:.

Discussion of the proposal continues in GitHub Discussion #1123.

The proposal lists four items as "still open, to be settled and published before the cutover proposal":.

The second item matters most to holders. The portal closes two years after launch, and the proposal doesn't yet say what happens to AKT that hasn't crossed by then. The final tally will confirm whether the plan goes ahead, but that answer, and the decisions in the votes that follow, will matter more to most holders than today's margin.

Recent findings suggest that — Allie Mellen has joined Microsoft as principal director for security research and threat intelligence. Mellen was previously a principal analyst at Forrester. She also wrote “Code War,” a book that explores cyberattacks as a powerful geopolitical weapon.

In her fresh role, Mellen said she will lead strategy for protection and threat intelligence, “helping shape what intelligence we produce, how AI can improve its speed and quality, and how we turn that knowledge into better protection for customers.”.

Sheriff was previously a vice president at DoorDash and has held leadership roles at Amazon, Starbucks and Parachute Home. His roles focused on customer experience, product growth, strategy and marketing.

“His skill set is the ideal background for charting how we attract customers and how we delight customers in this new age,” Jeff Seely, board chair for the Space Needle and Chihuly Garden and Glass, told the Seattle Times.

King is the founder and past CEO of Washington STEM, an organization that coordinates research, advocacy, policy, philanthropy and partnerships to support science, technology, engineering and math education in the state. She most recently served as a leader on the governing body of an international school in Luxembourg.

It has been revealed that wiltamuth joined Amazon in 2011 as an AWS vice president overseeing a large organization building developer and management tools. In 2018, he took a seven-month leave for colon cancer treatment. After returning, he sought a director-level position and thanked tech giant leaders for helping him find a better fit. “Their flexibility and creativity enabled me to extend my AWS career,” he mentioned.

Wiltamuth launched his tech career at Microsoft in 1993 and left nearly 19 years later as director of program management for Visual Studio Pro.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, amazon.com Inc.
  • According to recent reports, the firm didn’t disclose the terms of the deal.
  • In August, reports emerged that the tech giant had drawn takeover interest from Anthropic PBC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 20:40 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

In a recent development, amazon.com Inc. today revealed looks to hire the technical staff of startup Decart.AI Inc. and acquire its core technology.

According to recent reports, the firm didn’t disclose the terms of the deal. However, sources told Bloomberg that Amazon is paying about $7.5 billion. That’s nearly twice the valuation Decart reportedly received after its most recent funding round in May.

In August, reports emerged that the tech giant had drawn takeover interest from Anthropic PBC. The artificial intelligence provider reportedly sought to buy Decart for $6 billion but walked away from the deal in September. Rumors that Amazon could swoop in emerged the following month.

Decart founders Dean Leitersdorf, Moshe Shalev and Orian Leitersdorf will join the tech giant along with Decart’s research team. Additionally, Amazon is acquiring the technology behind the organization’s DOS platform, which helps boost the efficiency of AI models. Decart claims that the software can reduce the cost of some neural networks by a hundredfold.

The manufacturer hasn’t shared detailed information about how DOS works. However, the blog post in which Decart announced its May funding round did reveal that the platform optimizes AI models by “tuning the kernels.”.

In a recent development, kernels are the basic building blocks of neural networks. They’re relatively simple code snippets designed to run across a large number of chip cores. One common approach to optimizing them, kernel fusion, combines multiple kernels into a single code snippet that uses less hardware. In July, Decart disclosed that a custom model it had developed with DOS uses kernel fusion.

Sources indicate that the firm says that the platform also includes “proprietary compilers.” AI compilers translate neural networks into the platform-specific programming language of the host chip. They also optimize the models along they way. For example, the compiler that Amazon Web Services offers for its AWS Trainium machine learning chip uses quantization to compress models into a more memory-efficient form.

It’s unclear whether Decart positions DOS as an alternative to the default compilers provided with AI accelerators. According to Amazon, Decart has “worked closely” with its engineers since 2025 to optimize the performance of workloads deployed on its Trainium chips. The newest commercially available iteration of the chip, Tranium3, provides 2.52 petaflops of performance when processing FP8 data.

Amazon stated that the acquisition will help “further optimize both its inference and custom silicon performance.” According to the company, the goal is to not only speed up customers’ models but also lower their cost.

According to recent reports, “Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip,” said Peter DeSantis, Amazon’s senior vice president of foundational AI models, custom silicon and quantum computing. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.”.

Recent findings suggest that the acquisition doesn’t include Decart’s portfolio of internally developed AI models. Its two newest algorithms, Lucy 2.5 and Oasis 3, are world models that generate virtual environments based on prompts. The former algorithm is optimized for low-latency content creation, while the latter is designed to generate training data for robots.

  • The sketch, a fake commercial, stars host John Mulaney as a man who has found an easy way to care for his aging father without upending his own life: “Sister,” an “elder care system” that is free and is, in fact, his sister.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 18, 2026 at 1:23 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 1:23 pm.

A “Saturday Night Live” skit about caring for aging relatives touched a viral nerve after it aired over the weekend, including with Melinda French Gates, who offered her own “fact check” on the too-close-to-home comedy.

The sketch, a fake commercial, stars host John Mulaney as a man who has found an easy way to care for his aging father without upending his own life: “Sister,” an “elder care system” that is free and is, in fact, his sister.

French Gates wrote on Instagram this week that the sketch “is funny because it’s a little too true.” Using research from Pivotal, her investment and philanthropic organization, she went through the ad’s claims one by one and found that most held up:.

Recent findings suggest that sister will provide. True, French Gates said, citing AARP and the National Alliance for Caregiving. Among adults ages 55 to 64, women are nearly 40% more likely than men to care for an older relative, and nearly 40% more likely to provide constant care.

She’ll quit her job. “Mostly true,” at least the job part. Catalyst found that 42% of women who voluntarily left jobs in 2025 cited caregiving as the main reason.

According to recent reports, paid help is pricey. “True, unfortunately.” New America puts the average home health aide at more than $6,600 a month, and 24-hour care can top $25,000.

Sister may break down. Also true. In the Caregiving in the U.S. 2025 report, nearly two-thirds of caregivers mentioned they were under moderate or high emotional stress, and women felt the strain more than men did.

Recent findings suggest that “Free” is misleading. French Gates mentioned Sister isn’t free; she’s the one paying for the care, in lost wages, stalled careers, thinner retirement savings and less time for her own life.

French Gates has made women’s health and caregiving central to her work since she stepped down as co-chair of the Gates Foundation in 2024.

Industry observers note that she left with $12.5 billion to put toward her work on behalf of women and families. Much of that work runs through Pivotal, the Seattle-area organization she founded to handle her philanthropy and investments. In June she pledged another $215 million for women’s health, which brought her giving in that area to more than $600 million over two years. The pledge included $10 million to the Menopause Society for better menopause care in the U.S.

The sketch has been shared widely across the country this week, in part because it lines up so closely with the research.

In its own analysis, The Newly introduced York Times cited studies showing that daughters generally provide at least twice as much care to aging parents as sons do. The U.S., unlike many wealthy countries, offers no federal paid leave or long-term care insurance for family caregivers.

French Gates said she welcomed the conversation.

“I’m so glad we’re talking about this, and laughing about it,” she wrote on Instagram. “We need more honesty about what caring for loved ones really takes and why so much of that work falls to women. But I’d love for the day to come when these jokes don’t pack quite the same punch — because we’ve made it so much easier to care for the people we love.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Charles Hoskinson’s Cardano-linked privacy blockchain Midnight has inked a significant initial deal with a Japanese payments company as it aims to make further inroads into traditional finance.

The news comes soon after a key breakthrough for Midnight in the United Kingdom, where Monument Bank started tokenizing customer deposits on the blockchain.

Per a Nov. 19 NADA NEWS report, Midnight Foundation President Fahmi Syed noted the foundation had inked an MOU (memorandum of understanding) with a major Japanese payments company.

It has been revealed that syed did not name the company. But the deal is a big one for Midnight’s bid to establish a presence in Japan’s financial services sector.

However, it is just an initial agreement, and no commercial services have been rolled out in Japan yet.

It is also worth noting that the Midnight Foundation is talking to some major Japanese banks and companies working with intellectual property and medical data.

According to Syed, he spent two days in Tokyo meeting with major financial institutions and other companies.

Japan has been a key market for Midnight, along with the United States.

According to Midnight Foundation Japan country manager Taro Kimura, Japan is the only Asian country where the foundation has a local representative on the ground.

Midnight has been eyeing Japan more keenly due to the country’s sizeable Cardano community.

The Japanese push comes hot on the heels of a historic development in the British banking sector.

On Nov. 18, British financial institution Monument Bank started tokenizing retail customer deposits on Midnight. It is the first UK bank to launch such a product on a public blockchain.

Sources indicate that the first phase of the venture involves up to £250 million in tokenized deposits. For this, the bank is offering customers a 12-month fixed annual interest rate of 5.2%.

According to recent reports, midnight employs zero-knowledge cryptography to safeguard sensitive transaction details, unlike traditional public blockchains. As a result, banks can meet compliance requirements while keeping their customers’ private information and transaction details out of public view.

  • Terms of the deal were not disclosed this week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 18, 2026 at 2:03 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 2:03 pm.

Google is bringing Seattle-based Howie, maker of an AI scheduling assistant that works from your inbox, into its Google Labs division.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed this week. Google Labs, the tech giant’s experimental arm, declared the acquisition in a post on X, saying it “can’t wait to learn from them as we build the next generation of intuitive AI tools together for small businesses.”.

Howie CEO and co-founder Austin Petersmith noted on LinkedIn that the team will continue building Howie at Google. “Howie has always been built on top of Gmail and Google Calendar, so Google Labs is the perfect place for us to take this product to the next level,” he wrote.

Petersmith co-founded Howie around 2023 with CTO Dave Newman. The two first worked together in 2013 at Assembly, which Newman co-founded, and prototyped an AI assistant in 2015 before deciding the market wasn’t ready.

Sources indicate that we’re excited to welcome Howie to Google Labs! The @Howie_ai team has spent years figuring out scheduling and calendar management. We can’t wait to learn from them as we build the next generation of intuitive AI tools together for small businesses 🤝 https://t.co/8bzjebeGdD.

Users cc Howie on an email thread, and it coordinates meeting times, adds events to calendars, follows up as needed and flags scheduling conflicts. Customers set their own rules in an open-ended preferences document, such as “if it’s a pitch call, set it to 25 minutes and use Zoom.”.

Behind the scenes, Howie ran tasks through fine-tuned language models and looped in human scheduling experts when the AI wasn’t confident.

Howie raised a $6 million seed round led by True Ventures in September 2025, when it introduced publicly out of private beta. At the time, it had more than 1,000 paying customers, including startup founders, venture capitalists, recruiters, consultants and journalists, and was scheduling more than 5,000 meetings a week.

Industry observers note that the deal comes as Google and rivals including OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta race to build AI agents that complete tasks on behalf of customers. Google Labs acquired music generation platform ProducerAI earlier this year.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On-chain data indicates the attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses.
  • In a recent development, at the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot indicates its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT.
  • Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

On-chain data indicates the attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses.

In a recent development, at the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot indicates its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT. Binance's full zero-knowledge proof of those figures is due by Tuesday.

Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.

According to recent reports, blockchain intelligence firm Arkham has flagged the entity it tracks as "Binance Hacker" depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses. Arkham states those addresses "likely represent nested service(s)." These are third-party exchanges that use Binance for liquidity and custody, giving their own customers deposit addresses that sit on Binance's infrastructure.

It has been revealed that if Arkham is right, the hacker isn't depositing into an ordinary Binance account. The money would be going to smaller platforms that operate through Binance. Exchanges have long known this is a weak point for stolen funds moving into normal trading. Either way, Binance is now receiving stolen funds at its own deposit addresses while it works to show customers it has replaced what was taken.

Sources indicate that the FBI has attributed the October 29 theft to North Korea. The deposits come at a sensitive moment. Binance has just published its first reserve snapshot since the hack and has promised a full cryptographic proof of it by Tuesday.

$4 million is a small slice of a theft worth about $6.3 billion, but it matters for two reasons.

Sources indicate that it shows how the laundering works. Nested services are a common way into the regulated financial system. A third-party platform that relies on Binance for custody may run weaker identity checks on its own users. Funds deposited there can be swapped and withdrawn without the hacker ever opening a Binance account.

Binance can act on it. Binance can't freeze bitcoin and ether sitting in wallets nobody controls, and it doesn't control the stablecoins that issuers like Tether and Circle have frozen. Deposits that land at its own addresses are different: they are on Binance's platform, so Binance can freeze them itself. One of the first tests of how Binance handles the money still in the hacker's hands is whether it freezes these funds and identifies the services that own the addresses.

According to recent reports, while the hacker's funds move, Binance has been rebuilding its reserves. Its proof-of-reserves page now highlights:.

Recent findings suggest that the first page covers Binance's six largest assets. Customer balances are what users hold. Reserves are on-chain wallet balances, including assets held with outside custodians.

The second page has four more assets, and two of them stand out:.

Why USD1 and RLUSD matter: these are two of the stablecoins whose issuers froze stolen funds after the attack. World Liberty Financial froze $27 million of USD1, and Ripple began freezing RLUSD the same night. Both now show reserves above what Binance owes customers.

Assets with outside custodians: part of several reserves sits with outside custodians rather than in Binance's own exchange wallets:.

Asset | Held with third-party custodians.

In a recent development, the striking part isn't that the ratios reach 100%. It's how closely they stop there.

Sources indicate that compared with October's report: Binance's previous monthly report, published in early October before the hack, demonstrated BTC at 100.35% and USDT at 103.88%. ETH was already at exactly 100.00%. After the theft:.

It has been revealed that not every asset is that tight. USDC, ZEC and BNB carry buffers of 1.3% to 6%. The thinnest buffers are in BTC, ETH, USDT and SOL, which are among the assets the attacker took in the largest amounts.

How Binance notes it got here: the pattern fits Binance's account of replacing the stolen assets in stages. It reported 80% replaced on Friday, 90% on Saturday and 95% on Sunday. The remaining 5% is in less-liquid tokens it is still buying. The money came from:.

Binance confirmed taking 7,499 BTC from SAFU and has pledged to refill the fund to about $1 billion.

Recent findings suggest that what the snapshot can't show: it was taken a little over a day after the theft, once the rebuild was under way. It indicates the balance sheet after the replacement, not how large the gap was on October 29.

Industry observers note that binance indicates the full proof takes 40 to 50 hours to compute. Its latest upgrade says it will be ready "by Tuesday, 2026-11-03 (UTC)." The system is open source, in Binance's zkmerkle-proof-of-solvency repository.

What the proof guarantees, according to the project's circuit design document:.

The design also guards against a "dummy user attack" identified by Ethereum Foundation researcher Enrico Bottazzi. In that attack, fake accounts holding cheap tokens are used to offset debts in major assets.

What it doesn't prove: the reserve side. The project's verifier config describes the totals as information "published by CEX, it represents CEX's liability." The reserve figures are checked a different way, against the wallet addresses Binance publishes through the page's "Download All Address" option.

What customers can do: each user can get a Merkle proof for their account and check it against the published root. They can use the verifier code in Binance's repository rather than Binance's own interface. That doesn't prove Binance is solvent, but it confirms the user's balance was counted.

Binance has rebuilt its reserves to 100% across its ten largest assets, but on several of them the buffer is only a few coins. Meanwhile, stolen funds are reaching its deposit addresses through platforms that run on its infrastructure. Tuesday's proof can confirm customer balances. It can't show how Binance handles the stolen money arriving at its own door.

Zeno Power has hit a major milestone in its push to build nuclear batteries for underwater use.

According to recent reports, the startup stated today that it successfully demonstrated an electrically heated Stirling generator in a controlled maritime setting in Washington state. The two-week demonstration produced electrical power outputs in excess of 20 watts, said Lindsey Boles, Zeno’s chief product officer.

“It’s a really big step for us — just solidifying our expertise in how to design these, and then confirming our ability to translate that into operational hardware that meets or exceeds what our customers need,” Boles told GeekWire.

Zeno is developing the power system with support from the Department of Defense as a follow-up to an initial $7.5 million contract awarded in 2023. The generator uses a Stirling engine to convert heat into electricity by cycling gas through heating and cooling phases in a closed cylinder.

In a recent development, for the recent demonstration, the prototype device relied on an electric heating element. Future devices will instead rely on heat generated by the radioactive decay of strontium-90, a radioisotope that can be extracted from spent nuclear fuel.

According to recent reports, nuclear batteries have been in use for decades, primarily for space missions ranging from the Apollo moon shots to NASA’s Voyager spacecraft and Mars rovers. But the batteries being developed by Zeno Power promise to be at least four times more efficient than traditional radioisotope thermoelectric generators, Boles mentioned.

Industry observers note that boles noted the non-radiological test exceeded expectations. “There’s a difference between a design that works on paper and hardware that works in the field,” she said in a news release. “This is the moment our team has been building toward: proof that this technology works outside the lab.”.

Long-lasting nuclear batteries could be used to power undersea sensor networks or recharge autonomous underwater vehicles. “There are a lot of applications, especially on the maritime front, that we really want electricity for,” Boles noted. “And we really don’t need a ton of it. But we need it to be really reliable, and we need it to be long endurance, and we need it to be self-managed. … I think of it like a slow Tesla supercharger on the seabed.”.

According to recent reports, retired Navy Adm. John Richardson, former chief of naval operations and a member of Zeno’s board of directors, called the recent test an “key step toward undersea superiority.”.

Sources indicate that “Protecting maritime infrastructure and powering distributed systems at sea requires energy; energy that lasts for years, not days or months,” Richardson mentioned in a written statement. “As competition intensifies in contested domains, powered subsea systems will help keep us ahead. Zeno Power has steadily reduced risk, proven its technology, built a supply chain, and prepared to scale production.”.

According to recent reports, next year, Zeno Power aims to install a radioisotope heat source in its generator and test the system in a water tank under controlled laboratory conditions. If those tests are successful, Zeno will move forward with the first operational seabed deployment of its radioisotope-fueled maritime system later in 2027.

The maritime battery isn’t Zeno’s only product. The company is also working on a nuclear-powered heater system for spacecraft, with a demonstration on the lunar surface planned as early as 2028. Zeno’s broader vision is to provide long-lasting, reliable power on the moon and Mars, and in extreme environments on Earth.

Since its founding in 2018, Zeno has secured $105 million in private capital and has brought in $60 million in contracts with the Pentagon and NASA. The manufacturer has more than 95 employees at locations in Seattle, California and Washington, D.C., with the largest contingent working at its engineering headquarters in Seattle’s South Lake Union district.

Industry observers note that intesa’s XRP investment also grew over the same period to $27.2 million, driven mainly by 402,750 shares in the Bitwise XRP ETF. The manufacturer’s shares in the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF remained unchanged across both quarters.

Industry observers note that more broadly, the bank reduced its Bitcoin ETF exposure and increased SOL and XRP products. Most experts believe it follows the current market trend, and firms, especially traditional companies, need to diversify to make up for Bitcoin’s decline.

Historically, during bear phases, there’s a huge rotation of capital into altcoins, though it’s not sustained for long. As expected, Solana and XRP become institutional favorites, while Ethereum trades similarly to Bitcoin.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Ray is built into Exein Analyzer, the organization’s firmware security platform, which examines firmware for vulnerabilities, security weaknesses and compliance challenges.
  • In a recent development, the new offering is designed to address a growing security gap for manufacturers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 07:00 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Italian physical artificial intelligence cybersecurity manufacturer Exein SpA today debuted an AI agent called Ray that it claims can help manufacturers find the security weaknesses that matter most in their connected-device firmware.

Ray is built into Exein Analyzer, the organization’s firmware security platform, which examines firmware for vulnerabilities, security weaknesses and compliance challenges. Engineers can then use Ray to explore those findings in a conversational way, looking at the security posture of a single product or an entire fleet.

In a recent development, the new offering is designed to address a growing security gap for manufacturers. Some connected products contain thousands of software components, and a single scan of one can flag hundreds of potential issues, Exein stated. Which of those weaknesses actually needs to be fixed first is said to be the harder question.

Rather than working through separate vulnerability lists, security scores, trackers and compliance reports, engineers can put questions to Ray about Analyzer’s findings. Among the questions engineers can ask are what is driving a product’s security score, which vulnerabilities need attention first and which compliance challenges affect a firmware image.

To pick out the small number of issues that pose the greatest risk, Ray draws on Analyzer’s scan results, vulnerability reachability data and compliance findings. An explanation of why each matter matters is provided alongside the results. In cases where the same weakness appears across multiple products, Ray is said to help teams see when addressing one issue could improve security across an entire product line.

Exein is launching Ray after a run of attacks on connected infrastructure across Europe, including cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems that disrupted stores in several countries in October and November. Similar risks extend to industrial equipment, healthcare, energy and transport systems, according to the company.

According to recent reports, “Europe is connecting more of the physical world to software,” co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Giovanni Falcione said, “but too many products were never designed for the threat environment we have today. The recent attacks on refrigeration systems are a reminder that a weakness buried inside firmware can have consequences far beyond IT.”.

It has been revealed that the rate at which those weaknesses can be found and exploited is being “dramatically” accelerated by AI, Falcione said. With Ray, he said, engineering teams get a clearer way to work out what needs fixing before products reach the field, without every firmware engineer having to become a cybersecurity expert.

Sources indicate that also included in Ray is support for reading Analyzer’s findings against regulatory requirements such as the European Union’s Cyber Resilience Act. Reporting obligations under the act for actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents have applied since September, with the wider requirements taking effect in December 2027.

Industry observers note that founded in 2018, Exein offers technology that is distributed across more than 2 billion connected devices in sectors including industrial automation, automotive, energy, healthcare and robotics. The tech giant’s other offerings include Photon, which provides runtime security for connected devices, physical AI and autonomous AI agents. It raised $270 million at a $1.7 billion valuation in September.

In a recent development, ISTANBUL, Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Continuing to expand its presence across Europe with innovative electric and autonomous public transport solutions, Karsan has achieved another significant milestone in Italy with the introduction of its fresh 18-metre e-ATA Trolleybus. Karsan's Italian dealer, KMOBILITY, has won a tender issued by Bologna's public transport operator, TPER, and signed a contract for 35 units of the new e-ATA Trolleybus. The agreement also includes an option for an additional 35 vehicles, potentially bringing the total order to 70 units. Equipped with In Motion Charging (IMC) technology, which enables the vehicle to draw power from overhead lines while simultaneously charging its batteries, the new model demonstrates Karsan's technological expertise in developing electric public transport solutions that can adapt to different infrastructure requirements. Having ranked second in Italy's electric public transport market with a 12.5% market share in 2025, Karsan is further strengthening its position in Europe through this latest project in Bologna. Building on its role as a solution provider to TPER since 2022, when 24 e-ATA 18-metre electric buses were contracted, Karsan is set to expand its fleet within the operator's network to 59 vehicles with the new e-ATA Trolleybus, further reinforcing confidence in its products and technologies.

Combining Karsan's extensive engineering expertise in electric public transport with trolleybus technology, the latest e-ATA Trolleybus has been developed to meet the demands of busy urban routes, offering high passenger capacity and flexible energy management. The 18-metre model features In Motion Charging (IMC) technology, allowing it to operate using electricity supplied by overhead lines while simultaneously recharging its onboard batteries. With its high-capacity battery system, the e-ATA Trolleybus can operate entirely on electric power along routes without overhead lines, giving public transport operators greater flexibility in route planning. This enables operators to serve a wider transport network with the same vehicle, without being restricted to routes equipped with overhead lines. The technology also allows cities to make more efficient use of their existing trolleybus infrastructure, reduce the need for additional overhead line investments and extend electric public transport services to new routes.

High Passenger Capacity, Powerful Performance and Outstanding Comfort.

Industry observers note that karsan's new e-ATA Trolleybus combines high passenger capacity, powerful electric performance and outstanding comfort. The configuration developed for Bologna accommodates up to 146 passengers, with higher capacities available depending on customer requirements. Delivering peak torque of up to 22,000 Nm, the vehicle supports external DC charging at up to 200 kW in addition to charging through overhead lines, ensuring greater operational flexibility. Its four-door, fully low-floor design, spacious interior and accessibility features offer a comfortable and inclusive travel experience. Advanced driver assistance and safety technologies further enhance passenger and road safety. Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System (AVAS) enhances pedestrian safety by making the vehicle's presence more noticeable at low speeds. Additional safety features, including forward collision and pedestrian collision warnings, lane departure warning and traffic sign recognition, support drivers in navigating demanding urban traffic conditions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, asian stocks rallied on Tuesday after the board of Nvidia—the chipmaker at the center of the AI boom—voted Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, ending a leadership crisis that had battered the region’s AI supply chain. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), which makes Nvidia’s chips, surged 9.9%, the daily limit, adding 5.2 trillion Latest Taiwan dollars ($158 billion) to its market value in a single day.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 rose 3.9% as the market returned from a three-day weekend, while South Korea’s KOSPI surged 6.2% and Taiwan’s TAIEX climbed 9%.

It has been revealed that tuesday’s rally marks a rebound after a brutal stretch for the AI trade. The TAIEX fell by 17.5% last week, its worst such drop since 1991, pushing regulators to impose market stabilization measures, such as banning short selling, over the weekend.

According to recent reports, foxconn and Wistron, which assemble AI servers around Nvidia’s chips, rose almost 10%. SK Hynix, the world’s leading manufacturer of high-bandwidth memory, climbed 6.7%, while Samsung Electronics rose 6.6%. In Japan, Kioxia, Toshiba’s former memory chip unit, surged 10.0%, and Advantest, which makes chip-testing equipment, jumped 12.5%.

“This looks like a powerful relief rally, amplified by short covering and the sharp selloff that preceded it,” Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank, states. “The initial rebound could extend over the next few trading sessions, particularly in semiconductor-heavy markets such as Taiwan and South Korea, where earnings visibility has improved following [Jensen] Huang’s return.”.

Yet the relief from Huang’s return will likely peter out as broader concerns about the AI ecosystem persist. “I would expect markets to become more selective over the coming weeks, as investors shift their focus back from Nvidia’s leadership to AI spending, earnings delivery and the Fed’s policy outlook,” Chanana adds.

Not every Asian market is having a good day. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index fell by 0.6%. “The Hang Seng and mainland Chinese markets have struggled to find support,” claims Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone, a currency and derivatives broker. “Without a meaningful rotation back into Chinese AI and technology stocks, sustained upside looks challenging.”.

It has been revealed that huang’s return comes less than two weeks after his resignation. He stepped down on Nov. 12 after reports of multiple affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive who some U.S. intelligence officials believed was working with Chinese espionage, according to the Latest York Times.

Sources indicate that megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing company, is at the center of allegations that Nvidia chips were diverted to China. The company has denied the allegations.

Last week, the Commerce Department expanded export controls on AI processors to Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia and Brazil; it also closed a loophole that allowed Chinese companies to access Nvidia chips housed overseas.

In a recent development, on Monday, the department added seven companies to its Entity List, including Megaspeed. In a Federal Register notice, the department said the companies posed a “significant risk” and acted contrary to the “national security or foreign policy interests” of the U.S. The added companies include firms in Thailand, Malaysia, and Singapore, including several Megaspeed affiliates.

The same day, Nvidia’s board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang. “In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” the firm noted in a statement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 19, 2026 at 9:54 amNovember 19, 2026 at 10:10 am.

Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut today in a record $81.3 billion initial public offering, with big financial stakes for the Seattle area’s two tech giants.

According to recent reports, for Amazon, the IPO is a paper windfall. The organization started putting money into Anthropic in 2023, about $18 billion in all. At the $83 IPO price, its stake was worth about $161 billion. With Anthropic opening at $111.50 a share, that number was closer to $216 billion. The stock has since dropped below $100, which put Amazon’s stake under $200 billion.

Beyond the value of the investment, Anthropic is a major customer for Amazon’s cloud platform. The Claude maker has committed to spend at least $110 billion on Amazon Web Services through 2036.

For Microsoft, it’s more complicated. The Redmond firm agreed in late 2025 to invest up to $5 billion but hasn’t disclosed the size of its stake. Microsoft is buying $1 billion of Anthropic stock alongside the IPO, one of seven tech companies buying a combined $26 billion. Anthropic has committed to spend at least $47 billion on Microsoft’s Azure cloud through 2033.

But Microsoft is also pitching its own AI models against Anthropic’s, and it has been working to replace Anthropic’s models with OpenAI’s in some Copilot features, The Information reported this week.

It has been revealed that listing Anthropic’s compute partners on CNBC this morning, co-founder Daniela Amodei named Nvidia, Amazon, Google and Broadcom, but not Microsoft. Whether it was a slip or something more significant, it was an interesting omission.

A historic debut: The offering tops SpaceX’s $75 billion IPO in June, and it makes Anthropic the first standalone AI lab to go public, ahead of OpenAI.

The five-year-old manufacturer was valued at about $1.5 trillion at the $83 IPO price, on a fully diluted basis that counts employee stock and other shares not yet issued. The stock opened at $111.50, valuing Anthropic at about $2 trillion on the same basis. It has since traded as low as about $95.

Speaking before the opening bell, CEO Dario Amodei noted Anthropic will slow the training and release of its AI models for as long as it takes to be confident they’re safe, and that going public only strengthens that resolve.

“We will not bend to either business nor political pressure,” he said.

In an interview with CNBC’s Andrew Ross Sorkin afterward, Amodei called the push and pull between growth and that kind of restraint “one of the central tensions at the heart of the organization.”.

Anthropic is also a public benefit corporation, a structure that legally requires the company to balance shareholders’ interests with the public good.

Sources indicate that what’s next: Both Seattle-area giants have hedged their bets. Microsoft owns about 24% of OpenAI, and Amazon put $50 billion into OpenAI earlier this year.

OpenAI, which confidentially filed for its own IPO in June, is still aiming to go public in 2027.

Anthropic’s co-founders and some of its biggest shareholders are barred from selling for up to a year under the IPO’s lock-up rules, and Amazon has said it expects a customary lock-up period.

Amazon will update the value of its Anthropic holdings in its fourth-quarter results, much of it through earnings, which means the paper windfall is likely to boost Amazon’s fourth-quarter profit even though it hasn’t sold a share.

Tech Report: Yield-Bearing eZAR Blurs the Line Between Stablecoin and Investment Product

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1371 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that eZAR opened its rand-pegged token to the public on November 2 with R303 million in circulation.
  • In a recent development, most stablecoin debuts promise a token that never moves.
  • According to launch reports, eZAR is now open to the public and to fresh institutional partners after almost a year of pilot operations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

It has been revealed that eZAR opened its rand-pegged token to the public on November 2 with R303 million in circulation. Its reserve yield is the feature that puts the stablecoin label to the test.

In a recent development, most stablecoin debuts promise a token that never moves. eZAR's disclosures say its holders can make money or lose it. The rand-pegged token went live to the public on November 2, and its fine print reads more like an investment product than a payments coin.

According to launch reports, eZAR is now open to the public and to fresh institutional partners after almost a year of pilot operations. The firm says R303 million worth of tokens had been issued and were in circulation as of October 30.

In a recent development, the project is a partnership between eZAR Ltd, asset manager Ninety One and AVBOB Financial Services, with AVBOB acting as lead institution and liquidity partner. CEO Sean Emery said the team put "getting it right" ahead of "getting it massive" during the pilot. The message now is that eZAR is ready to scale.

The model also departs from the typical single-issuer coin. Neobanks, retailers, insurers and payment firms can plug the token into their own branded wallets and share in the economics. Transfers between participating wallets settle within seconds at any hour and, according to the organization, cost nothing.

In a recent development, the reserves backing eZAR are invested through a money market strategy run by Ninety One, mainly in the Ninety One Money Market Fund. Returns are distributed daily to partners after partnership fees, and each partner then decides on what terms its own customers receive a share.

Recent findings suggest that ninety One's head of digital assets, Adam Duxbury, described it as upcoming rails under an old discipline. His firm has run money market strategies for 25 years, he mentioned, and South Africa should build its own digital rand rather than import a dollar coin.

The framing is clever, since it presents the yield as a feature of "digital cash that can grow." Yet that same feature makes the classification question hard to avoid.

In a recent development, the risk language is the most revealing part of the launch. eZAR describes itself as a crypto asset issued by the eZAR En Commandite Partnership. It states that the token is not legal tender, not a bank deposit and not a banking product, and that it carries no guarantee.

According to recent reports, the details that follow set it further apart. The R1 redemption value depends on available liquidity. Money market returns can be positive or negative, so capital is at risk. Holders also own no units in the underlying fund and have no direct claim on it.

"Capital at risk" rarely appears in stablecoin terms. A payments token is meant to hold its value and let customers redeem at par, yet eZAR's own documents hedge on both counts. Back in March, a market survey from Blockhouse had already noted that eZAR doesn't qualify as a stablecoin under most regulations. The live launch now tests that observation against a real product.

In a recent development, in the major rulebooks, the yield is the sticking point. The US GENIUS Act bars permitted payment stablecoin issuers from paying holders any form of interest or yield solely for holding, using or retaining the token. The EU's MiCA framework takes a similar line on interest. The logic is that a payment token paying a return starts to function like an unregulated deposit.

The OCC issued its final GENIUS Act rules on October 21, and they confirmed that ban for covered issuers. The contested ground lies elsewhere, in who sits between the issuer and the holder. Earlier OCC proposals set a rebuttable presumption against yield arrangements run through affiliates and related third parties, whereas the statute itself names only issuers.

It has been revealed that eZAR's design lands squarely in that gray zone. Returns flow to partners, and the partners decide how customers share in them. Whether that amounts to an issuer paying yield or a partner passing on profit is precisely the kind of question US regulators are now wrestling with, and it would be a difficult one to argue before the OCC.

In a recent development, eZAR doesn't operate under the US or EU regimes, so none of those rules apply to it directly. eZAR Ltd is described as an authorised financial services provider responsible for the main technology and services behind the partnership. That technology also draws on the South African Reserve Bank's Project Khokha 2, where eZAR's parent firm, Block Markets Africa, was a technical contributor.

This background signals a serious, institution-backed build rather than a speculative launch. Even so, the rand stablecoin field is getting crowded. ZARU introduced earlier this year as an institutional-grade rand coin, and a pattern is emerging of different models competing for the same local payments niche.

Sources indicate that the bigger question is whether South Africa will define stablecoins narrowly, as the US and EU do, or leave room for hybrid products like this one. Because the network is permissioned, the reported circulation figure also rests on organization disclosure rather than a public ledger, which makes the regulatory and disclosure framework matter even more.

According to recent reports, for everyday customers, the appeal is easy to see. A rand token that moves in seconds, costs nothing to send and might earn a daily return makes an attractive pitch. For partners, shared infrastructure with a revenue share offers a way into digital payments without building a coin from scratch.

According to recent reports, the trade-off sits in the disclaimers. A holder who treats eZAR like a bank balance could be caught off guard by liquidity-dependent redemption, or by a money market return that dips below zero. That gap between how the product feels and how it is legally defined is where regulators tend to step in.

eZAR is best understood as a hybrid: a payments token with an investment return attached. It may well succeed on those terms. Still, as more jurisdictions tighten the stablecoin definition around no-yield, par-redemption tokens, products like this will increasingly be judged on what they are rather than what they are called. How South African regulators treat eZAR in the coming months will show which way that debate is heading.

#167705. Latest Update: Why is gas suddenly cheaper? Five factors driving the drop to $3.64 a gallon

Latest Update: Why is gas suddenly cheaper? Five factors driving the drop to $3.64 a gallon

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (831 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fortune

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The average price of gasoline in the U.S.
  • Sources indicate that context, of course, matters.
  • According to recent reports, “The scale of decline has been a little bit surprising,” said Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The average price of gasoline in the U.S. has plunged nearly 90 cents a gallon in two months down to its lowest level since the early days of the Iran war, coming just in time for Thanksgiving travel.

Sources indicate that context, of course, matters. The average price for a gallon of regular unleaded was $3.64 on Monday. Though that’s 57 cents higher than the price a year ago, according to AAA, it has come down precipitously of late. And it would only hace to fall a bit further to $3.58 to hit where it stood on Thanksgiving Day 2022. Over the weekend, in some parts of the country, prices at the pump could be seen hovering at—or occasionally even below—the $3 mark, a huge psychological break for consumers who have suffered through years of rising prices.

According to recent reports, “The scale of decline has been a little bit surprising,” said Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy. “But, given how things have developed, it’s not really a shock.”.

Industry observers note that so, why have prices fallen so sharply since late September? It’s a combination of geopolitical factors in the Middle East, typical seasonal declines, and refinery operational issues. And, no, there wasn’t any conspiracy to keep prices higher ahead of the midterm elections. However, President Donald Trump’s actions are key contributors.

Here are the five main factors causing fuel prices—especially gasoline—to tumble:.

Despite some ongoing conflict, the combination of U.S. naval escorts, complicated oil tanker transfers, and pipeline bypass routes have allowed the Middle East to return to nearly 90% of its pre-war oil exports, even though prices remain elevated from high tanker contracting and insurance costs. The rising levels of oil exports—despite depleted strategic oil reserves worldwide—have helped the global oil benchmark dip slightly below $90 per barrel as of Monday.

Prior to the elections, Trump openly mentioned he was delaying any major ramp-up in attacks until after the midterms. That warning was keeping oil prices inflated as oil markets anticipated more disruptions to global oil flows in November. While risks remain and no peace deal seems on the near-term horizon, the lack of an escalation has helped prices fall. “The biggest thing now is this looming uncertainty over whether there will be something concrete and long-lasting,” De Haan told Fortune.

From a simple supply-and-demand standpoint, fuel prices typically peak in the summer during the busy driving season and bottom out in the winter when more people are bundled up at home. Although there are brief travel spikes for Thanksgiving and Christmas, driving is typically muted near the end and beginning of each calendar year. Likewise, fuel is cheaper to manufacture during the colder months. Summer-grade gasoline is more expensive because of extra additives required to keep fuel components from evaporating in the heat. Winter-grade fuel is cheaper and less complex.

Industry observers note that globally, nearly 10% of refineries remain offline, largely in the Middle East and Russia because of wars. But, in the U.S., there also were supply disruptions at ExxonMobil’s Joliet and Phillips 66’s Wood River refineries in Illinois. Those temporary outages from weather complications and mechanical failures caused additional price spikes throughout the Midwest. “The refining issues were boosting prices ahead of the election,” De Haan said. “As these issues have been getting resolved, they’ve been pushing prices down, coupled with the seasonality, coupled with oil markets.” Outside of the Middle East and Russia, China also had mothballed some refineries during the Iran war. As China has depleted more of its own reserves, the country has of late ramped up its output, including its fuel exports, adding to global supplies.

Refining complexes aren’t built to operate like light switches for diesel or other petroleum products. When refineries are pushed to run at their maximum utilization levels for diesel, that also means increasing their volumes of gasoline. With diesel demand surging in the fall, the U.S refining industry is on overdrive and raking in record profits, often delaying planned maintenance work until next year. “Refineries are operating at their highest November rate since 1998,” De Haan said. “This may be the highest utilization year for refineries ever. It’s going to be really close.”.

Industry observers note that fuel prices remain elevated, but there’s no hiding how far they’ve fallen. As such, nearly as many Americans as last year proposal to travel for Thanksgiving. AAA projects 72.9 million people will travel on the road this Thanksgiving, only a slight drop from 73.1 million last year.

Recent findings suggest that gasBuddy’s survey data showed that almost two-thirds of Americans plan to hit the road this week. Close to 20% of travelers mentioned they will cut back on other holiday spending to cover the extra fuel costs.

If there are no more major energy disruptions in the Middle East, De Haan said, the national average for gasoline could bottom out as low as $3.35 per gallon over the next few weeks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in Matt Dinniman’s previous career, he sold whimsical cat prints on Etsy. Now he writes bestselling books in his underwear while snacking on Twizzlers. Dinniman, a 52-year-old father of four, is the author of the “Dungeon Crawler Carl” series, which has sold more than 20 million copies across eight books, according to The Wall Street Journal. The series follows a guy competing on an alien game show.

Industry observers note that that loyal following gave him leverage later. Dinniman struck a rare deal that lets him keep control of his e-books while Penguin Random House handles print and Audible handles audio. The audiobooks alone have sold 10 million copies, and a TV series begins filming in 2027.

“It’s insane,” Dinniman says of his success. But fame has its drawbacks. Dinniman, 52, is moving to a gated community near Tucson, Arizona, partly because fans keep showing up at his door. “I’m glad it’s happened to me later in life because I don’t think I’ll ever get used to it,” he adds.

Breaking: Uncommon Thinkers: Andrew Redd’s audacious proposal to turn ocean volcanoes into power plants

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 19, 2026 at 10:07 amNovember 19, 2026 at 4:42 pm.
  • In a recent development, editor’s note: This series profiles five Seattle-area “Uncommon Thinkers,” who will be recognized Dec.
  • Andrew Redd‘s career path creates a tidy narrative: grow up in Seattle steeped in aviation and maritime culture, study mechanical engineering and aerospace, work at SpaceX, then launch an offshore geothermal energy startup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 19, 2026 at 10:07 amNovember 19, 2026 at 4:42 pm.

In a recent development, editor’s note: This series profiles five Seattle-area “Uncommon Thinkers,” who will be recognized Dec. 10 at the GeekWire Gala in partnership with Greater Seattle Partners.

Andrew Redd‘s career path creates a tidy narrative: grow up in Seattle steeped in aviation and maritime culture, study mechanical engineering and aerospace, work at SpaceX, then launch an offshore geothermal energy startup.

The dots connect, but the picture they form is anything but ordinary: bold in vision, fast in execution and enormous in potential.

Redd has next-level ambition, and he’s directing it at solving one of the world’s biggest and most urgent problems — adding renewable, massively scalable energy that can outcompete fossil fuels and reach the grid quickly enough to make a difference in the race against climate change.

According to recent reports, underwater geothermal energy has never been tapped in a significant way, but to Redd, the idea was irresistible. “It checks all of the boxes for our perfect future energy source,” he remarked.

Sources indicate that he founded Endurance Energy on the north shore of Seattle’s Lake Union in January 2025, and this September the team oversaw its fifth deep-sea deployment. At a site 300 miles off the Oregon coast, its prototype system generated more electricity than it consumed. The startup has raised $63 million from investors and has roughly three dozen employees.

It has been revealed that nate Bek, a principal at Ascend, praised Redd’s ability to attract “brilliant” talent in pursuit of his goal. The Seattle venture firm is one of the startup’s early backers.

“I’ve been deeply inspired by what [Redd]’s building at Endurance and haven’t shut up about it since the day we met,” Bek stated. “He somehow makes powering the world from the bottom of the ocean feel inevitable, all while remaining remarkably measured and transparent about the progress.”.

For Redd, studying engineering and aerospace in college was so clear-cut that it wasn’t a choice at all. Growing up around Boeing, seaplanes, the Museum of Flight and the Pacific Northwest’s rich maritime industry naturally pointed him toward those sectors. He wanted a degree as expansive as his influences.

Recent findings suggest that “I didn’t really want to have to choose whether it was going to be boats or space travel or airplanes,” he said. “I just wanted to be able to do anything — keep the world as wide open as possible.”.

After graduating from Princeton University, Redd worked at Neuralink, an Elon Musk company developing technology that lets the brain communicate directly with computers. A year later, in 2021, he moved to Musk’s rocket company, SpaceX.

That was another no-duh decision, as Redd viewed it.

“I saw SpaceX as really the place to be, where early-career people are given the most amount of resources and responsibility, and that felt like the fastest way to learn and the most engaging possible scenario to be in,” Redd said. “I wanted to be tossed into something that was a little bit crazy.”.

It has been revealed that redd joined as SpaceX was starting to build its first orbital Starship rockets. The program brought together passionate young people and experienced SpaceX engineers who served as mentors. Wild ideas were entertained and explored. Everyone was committed to the mission. It was just the experience Redd wanted, and he planned to stick around for seven to 10 years.

Then artificial intelligence started booming.

In 2024, the build-out of sprawling, energy-hungry data centers for AI was accelerating with no end in sight. At the same time, efforts to electrify transportation, heating and cooling were driving up demand for power. Redd saw these trends sparking a surge in new natural gas generation, locking in decades of carbon emissions.

He wanted to find a better way. He went into engineering mode, focusing on all the essential criteria for an energy source: it had to be clean, not dependent on intermittent sun or wind, capable of producing massive amounts of energy, readily deployable, subject to fewer regulatory hurdles than something like nuclear, economically competitive, and scalable.

Redd recognized the tremendous heat contained under Earth’s surface as a terrific source for renewable energy and realized that most of the world’s active volcanoes are offshore. The unknown was whether the rocky ocean floor would be suitable for geothermal wells, so he did some research and found publications from geology experts who said the conditions would be “perfect.”.

“You can tell,” he said, “when there’s a moment in time that you need to go and reach out and grab something, and that was really my impression — if I didn’t start this now, this would never come into existence, or wouldn’t come into existence soon enough to make a meaningful impact.”.

Recent findings suggest that in launching Endurance, Redd was intentional about the culture he wanted to create. He was aiming for a multidisciplinary group of mission-driven employees eager to collaborate and learn from each other: top talent that would attract more of the same and make Endurance a place people were excited to work.

“The hardest part of an early-stage startup is recruiting,” Redd stated, “especially if you’re a first-time founder.”.

The startup employs about a dozen SpaceX alumni, plus employees from the fusion company Helion Energy and the aerospace venture Blue Origin.

Recent findings suggest that A strong team is key to Endurance’s success. That’s because, enthusiasm and passion aside, the startup faces steep engineering and economic challenges. The technology must withstand high pressure, corrosive conditions and mineral scaling inside devices, and seafloor machinery could be costly to repair. The systems will need expensive subsea cables to carry power to shore over potentially long distances. It’s a heavy lift.

While the September sea trial didn’t go perfectly, Redd is happy with the results. The firm landed its 3-ton power plant on the seafloor near a natural vent and produced net energy from it — albeit for only 8.7 seconds. Technical difficulties and a power-cable failure cut the dive short.

It has been revealed that team members successfully operated the system remotely from Seattle through a fiber-optic network running along the seabed. Redd remarked he’s grateful for access to the network, which is part of the National Science Foundation’s Regional Cabled Array and operated by the University of Washington.

Sources indicate that endurance engineers also drilled what they called the world’s first subsea geothermal well at a site about 5,000 feet below the ocean’s surface. The 2-inch-wide, 52-foot-deep well delivered hydrothermal fluid, but the flow was too restricted to run the power plant, sending the team to the natural vent.

Redd said there’s a lot of work ahead, but the team “made huge strides” in learning and in reducing the project’s risks.

The company now is developing Leopard, its 2-megawatt generator. After testing the technology at the research site off the Oregon coast, Endurance aims to deliver power from a Leopard system in Tonga next year as its first commercial project. Subsea geothermal energy could ultimately reduce the island nation’s reliance on imported diesel and put the startup one step closer to its objective of generating terawatts of planet-friendly energy.

“This was always the end goal,” Redd mentioned. “Create something that is highly meaningful for the world.”.

Editor’s Note: Nate Bek of Ascend is a former GeekWire reporter.

Women’s football has a $1 billion opportunity—and the WSL wants a slice of the pie

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1050 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fortune

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the 1999 FIFA Women’s World Cup final was a watershed moment for women’s football, with record-breaking attendance and viewership numbers.
  • Recent findings suggest that since then, interest in women’s football has grown significantly.
  • Now CEO of Women’s Super League Football, the firm responsible for operating the top two English women’s leagues (WSL and WSL2), Doucet is at the sharp end of that opportunity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the 1999 FIFA Women’s World Cup final was a watershed moment for women’s football, with record-breaking attendance and viewership numbers. More than 40 million people in North America tuned in to watch the U.S. beat China 5–4 on penalties in the final. Among them was ­ Canadian Nikki Doucet, then a student and college basketball player at St. Francis Xavier University. “That was the first time I’d seen women’s team sports on TV, and I remember feeling so excited,” she says.

Recent findings suggest that since then, interest in women’s football has grown significantly. Its global fan base is projected to surpass 800 million by 2030, according to Nielsen Sports, while Fifpro expects the sport to be a $1 billion industry by 2027—a 72% increase from 2024.

Now CEO of Women’s Super League Football, the firm responsible for operating the top two English women’s leagues (WSL and WSL2), Doucet is at the sharp end of that opportunity. England has become a commercial force in women’s football: Eight of the world’s 15 highest-revenue clubs are in the WSL, according to Deloitte, and Doucet believes the league is well-positioned to capture a “significant portion” of the potential $1 billion the sport is predicted to generate.

According to recent reports, american entrepreneurs and investment groups are taking note. The success of the Women’s National Basketball Association—now an $850 million franchise— underlines the potential, and many see an opportunity to buy in at an early stage in the commercial development of the sport.

U.S. businesswoman Michele Kang bought the London City Lionesses in 2023, leading the club to its 2025 WSL promotion. Other notable investors include Reddit cofounder Alexis Ohanian, who holds a minority stake in Chelsea FC Women, and U.S. financier Marc Zahr, an investor in Aston Villa Women.U.S. businesswoman Michele Kang bought the London City Lionesses in 2023, leading the club to its 2025 WSL promotion. Other notable investors include Reddit cofounder Alexis Ohanian, who holds a minority stake in Chelsea FC Women, and U.S. financier Marc Zahr, an investor in Aston Villa Women.

Speaking at the WSL’s Upcoming Playbook ­ summit earlier this year, one investor argued that European women’s football represented the “best opportunity in sport,” on a risk-adjusted basis.

“I think of my career as if I’m still an athlete. I practice for every board meeting in the same way that I used to train for a game. Your practice should be so hard, the game is easy.”.

According to recent reports, “The enterprise value of these clubs is 100% going up,” Doucet, a former investment banker at Citi, says. “The question is, do you have owners that want to participate in this asset class of women’s football? There are different tradeoffs versus men’s football and different risk factors because we’re in a different stage of development.”.

Doucet’s challenge is turning rising global interest in the women’s game into regular paying customers. There was a surge in interest following the England Lionesses’ UEFA Women’s Euro 2022 victory: Average attendance at WSL matches tripled to 5,616 the following season. But last year, median attendance was 3,236—and it remains heavily concentrated in a few clubs.

It has been revealed that “This isn’t a manufacturing challenge. This is a marketing and revenue challenge,” Doucet says. The league invested in a rebrand of both the WSL and WSL2 ahead of the newly expanded league this season, and clubs are also investing more. In April, WSL team Brighton announced plans to build Europe’s first purpose- built women’s football stadium at an estimated cost of more than £75 million ($99 million).

In a recent development, “You have to invest in building the foundations that will generate long- term returns, but they might take time until you actually see the results,” Doucet notes. “That’s the constant tradeoff.”.

Industry observers note that the underlying economics also remain fragile. Despite the high revenues, only four of the 14 clubs in the WSL recorded a profit (two clubs did not publish detailed financial data). The league itself, which is co-owned by the participating clubs, posted an operating loss of £8.2 million ($10.8 million) for the year ending July 2025.

Sources indicate that doucet attributes much of the loss to one-off costs associated with becoming an independent business, including establishing its own HR, finance, legal, and regulatory teams. The WSL and WSL2 formally split from the Football Association (FA) in 2024, shortly after Doucet joined the organization. She states the league is now profitable, although declined to share the financial details.

“We’re in a transition phase, which is probably a little bit messy. The challenge is going from big structural moments, like a World Cup, to building a weekly fan habit around women’s professional football,” Doucet says.

Sources indicate that the majority of the league’s revenues so far have come from broadcast rights and commercial partnerships. The league generated £8.7 million ($11.5 million) from Sky and the BBC in 2025, and the league counts Doucet’s former employer Nike, in addition to Airbnb, Apple, and ­ Barclays, among its growing list of sponsors.

Industry observers note that the opportunities for commercial sponsors are different from those in the men’s sport, Doucet says. “We have a different audience that really values companies that are investing in women’s football,” she says. “They’re very brand loyal, and they show much deeper engagement.”.

Doucet’s current priority is improving the spectacle on the pitch. “The fans want to watch the best players, and they want to watch a competition that’s exciting and has jeopardy,” she claims. Good progress has been made in this area, too. The London City Lionesses signed three-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas from Barcelona this summer, and the WSL had the highest representation of players at last year’s Women’s Euro tournament of any league.

Ensuring the WSL’s longevity is a responsibility Doucet is acutely aware of. “This isn’t a five-year business,” she says. “This is a generational asset.” She remains optimistic about what lies ahead. Doucet adds: “We’re in an early stage, so the potential is almost completely untapped—you don’t know how major it could be.”.

This article appears in the December 2026/January 2027 problem of Fortune with the headline “Women’s football has a $1 billion opportunity—and the WSL wants a slice of the pie.”.
